16:110: Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Yazid Al-Muqri' narrated to us, Haywah and others narrated to us, they said: Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman Abu Al-Aswad narrated to us, he said: A mission was sent to the people of Madinah, so I registered for it, then I met Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, and I informed him, but he forbade me from that emphatically, he said: Ibn Abbas informed me that some people from the Muslims were with the polytheists, and they were increasing in number during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and an arrow would come and hit one of them, killing him or striking his neck and killing him, so God revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves, and Al-Layth narrated it from Abu Al-Aswad. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ramadi narrated to us, Abu Ahmad, meaning Al-Zubayri, narrated to us, Muhammad bin Sharik Al-Makki narrated to us, Amr bin Dinar narrated to us from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, he said: There were people from the people of Makkah who converted to Islam and they were hiding their Islam, so the polytheists expelled them with them on the day of Badr, and some of them were afflicted by the actions of others. The Muslims said: Our companions were Muslims and they were forced, so ask forgiveness for them. Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves 10:13. Ikrimah said: So he wrote to those Muslims who remained with this verse: They have no excuse. He said: So they went out, and the polytheists caught up with them, so they gave them taqiyya, so this verse was revealed: And among the people is he who says, ‘We believe in God’ 10:13. Akrima said: This verse was revealed about young men from Quraysh who spoke about Islam in Mecca, including Ali bin Umayya bin Khalaf, Abu Qais bin Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, Abu Al-Aas bin Munabbih bin Al-Hajjaj, and Al-Harith bin Zam’ah. Ad-Dahhak said: It was revealed about some hypocrites who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca and went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr, and were afflicted among those who were afflicted. So this noble verse was revealed in general regarding everyone who stayed among the polytheists, and was able to emigrate but was not able to establish the religion, so he is unjust to himself and committing a sin by consensus, and by the text of this verse, where God Almighty says: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves meaning by abandoning emigration They will say, ‘In what state were you?’ meaning why did you stay here and abandon emigration They will say, ‘We were oppressed in the land.’ meaning we were not able to leave the country, nor go about the land They will say, ‘Was not the earth of God spacious?’ The verse. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad bin Dawud bin Sufyan told us, Yahya bin Hassan, Sulayman ibn Musa Abu Dawud told us, Ja`far ibn Sa`d ibn Samra ibn Jundub told us, Khabib ibn Sulayman told me on the authority of his father Sulayman ibn Samra, on the authority of Samra ibn Jundub, and after that, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever gathers with a polytheist and lives with him is like him. Al-Suddi said: When Al-Abbas, Uqayl and Nawfal were taken captive, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Abbas: Redeem yourself and your nephew. He said: O Messenger of God, have we not reached your qiblah and witnessed your testimony? He said: O Abbas, you have argued and you have disputed. Then he recited to him this verse: Was not the earth of God spacious? The verse was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And His saying: Except for the weak to the end of the verse, this is an excuse from God for these people to not emigrate, and that is because they are not able to escape from the hands of the polytheists, and if they were able they would not know how to take the path, and for this reason He said: They are not able to devise a plan nor are they guided to a way, Mujahid, Ikrimah and Al-Suddi said: He means a path. And the Almighty said: Then it is those whom God may pardon, meaning that God will forgive them for not emigrating. Perhaps is a requirement, and God is Pardoning and Forgiving. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu’aym told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying the ‘Isha’ prayer, he said: God hears whoever praises Him. Then he said before prostrating: “O God, save ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, O God, save Salamah ibn Hisham, O God, save al-Walid ibn al-Walid, O God, save the weak among the believers, O God, make your punishment severe upon Mudar, O God, make them years like the years of Joseph.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Muammar al-Muqri told us, Abdul-Warith told us, Ali ibn Zaid told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands after he had finished the salutation while facing the qiblah, and said: O God, save al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, Salamah ibn Hisham, and the weak Muslims who are unable to devise a plan and are not guided to a path from the hands of the disbelievers. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told us, Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zaid, on the authority of Abdullah or Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Qurashi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate after the noon prayer: O God, save al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, and the weak Muslims from the hands of the polytheists who are unable to devise a plan and are not guided to a path. This hadith has a witness in the Sahih from another chain of transmission, as mentioned above. Abdul Razzaq said: Ibn Uyaynah informed us on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: My mother and I were among the weak among women and children. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Al-Nu’man informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Abu Malikah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, except the weak, he said: My mother and I were among those whom God Almighty excused. And his saying: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God will find on the earth many [alternative] locations and abundance, this is an incitement to emigrate and an encouragement to separate from the polytheists, and that wherever the believer goes he will find a way out and a refuge in which to fortify himself. Al-Maraghim is a noun, and the Arabs say: So-and-so is opposing his people, opposing and opposing. Al-Nabigha ibn Ja’dah said: Like a mountain, the dear one who is reluctant and the one who escapes seeks refuge in its corners Ibn Abbas said: Maraghim means moving from one land to another. This was also narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Ath-Thawri. Mujahid said: Maraghim Katheer means moving away from what he dislikes. Sufyan bin Uyaynah said: Maraghim Katheer means towers. What appears - and God knows best - is that it is the protection that one fortifies oneself with and uses to resist the enemy. His saying ample means provision, this was said by more than one of them, including Qatada, where he said: In His saying: He will find on the earth many [alternative] places and abundance meaning from misguidance to guidance, and from scarcity to wealth, and His saying: And whoever emigrates for the sake of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon God meaning whoever emigrates for the sake of God and His Messenger and dies on the way, then he has attained the reward of the one who emigrated, as is proven in the two Sahihs and other Sahihs, Musnads and Sunans on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Ansari on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, on the authority of `Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Actions are but by intentions, and each person will have but what he intended. So whoever emigrated for the sake of God and His Messenger, then his emigration is for the sake of God and His Messenger. And whoever emigrated for a worldly gain or a woman to marry, then his emigration is for what he emigrated for.” This is general in emigration and in all actions. And from it is the authentic hadith in the two Sahihs about the man who killed ninety-nine people, then the worshipper completed the hundred and then asked a scholar: Is there any repentance for him? He said to him: Who is standing between you and repentance? Then he advised him to move from his country to another country where he would worship God. So when he left his country as a migrant to the other country, death overtook him on the way, so the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. Some said: He came repentant, and others said: He had not arrived yet. So they were ordered to measure the distance between the two lands, so whichever one he was closer to would be from it. So God ordered this one to come closer to this one, and this one to move away, so they found him closer to the land to which he had migrated by a handspan, so the angels of mercy took him. And in another narration, when death came to him, he turned his chest away to the land to which he had migrated. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Atik, on the authority of his father Abdullah bin Atik, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever leaves his home to fight in the cause of God, and then says: Where are those who fight in the cause of God? And he falls from his mount and dies, his reward is with God, or he is bitten by an mount and dies, his reward is with God, or he dies a natural death, his reward is with God - meaning a natural death in his bed. By God, this is a statement that I did not hear from any of the Arabs before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - and whoever kills a camel deserves Paradise.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Shaiba al-Hizami told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mughirah al-Khuzami told me, on the authority of al-Mundhir ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: Khalid ibn Hizam emigrated to the land of Abyssinia and was bitten by a snake on the road and died, so the following verse was revealed about him: “And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon God. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Al-Zubayr said: So I was expecting him and waiting for his arrival while I was in the land of Abyssinia, and nothing saddened me as much as the sadness of his death when it reached me, because few of those who emigrated from Quraysh were without some of their family or relatives with them, and there was no one with me from Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza, and I do not hope for anyone other than him. This trace is very strange, for this story is Meccan, and the revelation of this verse is Medinan, so perhaps he meant that it was revealed to include his ruling with others, even if that was not the reason for the revelation, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, the client of Abdullah ibn Ja`far, told us, Sahl ibn `Uthman told us, `Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman told us, Ash`ath, who is Ibn Suwar, told us, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Damrah ibn Jundub went out to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he died on the way before he reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the verse, And whoever emigrates from his home to God and His Messenger was revealed. My father told us, `Abdullah ibn Raja` told us, Israel informed us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu Damrah ibn al-`Ays al-Zarqi, who was blind and was in Mecca. When the verse, Except for the weak among men, women and children who are unable to devise a plan was revealed, I said: I am rich, and I am able to devise a plan. So he prepared himself, intending to go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but death overtook him in al-Tan`im, so this verse was revealed: And whoever emigrates from his home to God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him was revealed. Al-Tabarani said: Al-Hasan bin Arubah Al-Basri told us, Haywah bin Shureih Al-Himsi told us, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, Ibn Thawban told us on the authority of his father, Makhul told us on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ghanam Al-Ash'ari, Abu Malik told us, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "God said: Whoever volunteers to go out in My cause to fight, seeking My countenance, believing in My promise, and believing in My messengers, then he is under God's guarantee. Either He takes him with the army and admits him into Paradise, or he returns under God's guarantee. And if he pursues a slave and annoys him until he returns him to his family with whatever reward he has earned, or spoils, and gains from God's bounty and he dies, or is killed, or his horse or camel kicks him, or a snake bites him, or he dies in his bed by whatever death God wills, then he is a martyr." Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Baqiyah from the bounty of God to the end, and he added after his words: then he is a martyr, and Paradise is for him. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Ibrahim bin Ziyad Sublan told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Hamid bin Abi Hamid, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yazid al-Laithi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever goes out for Hajj and dies, the reward of the pilgrim will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever goes out for Umrah and dies, the reward of the pilgrim will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever goes out to fight in the cause of God and dies, the reward of the fighter will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection.” This is a strange hadith from this source. These are another group who were oppressed in Mecca and humiliated by their people, so they agreed with them in the sedition. Then they were able to escape by emigrating, so they left their country, their families and their wealth seeking the pleasure and forgiveness of God, and they joined the ranks of the believers, and fought with them against the disbelievers, and were patient. So God the Almighty informed us that after that, that is, that action, which is the response to the sedition, He is Forgiving and Merciful to them on the Day of their Resurrection. The Day every soul will come to argue that is, argue for itself no one will argue on its behalf, neither a father nor a son nor a brother nor a wife. And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has done that is, of good and evil and they will not be wronged that is, the reward for good will not be reduced, nor will the reward for evil be increased, nor will they be wronged even a speck.
16:1: God Almighty tells us about the approach of the Hour and its nearness, using the past tense, which indicates certainty and inevitable occurrence, as in His saying: The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away, and He said: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And his saying: So do not hasten it meaning that what is far is near, so do not hasten it. It is possible that the pronoun refers to God, and it is possible that it refers to the torment, and both are related, as God Almighty said: "And they urge you to hasten the punishment. And were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them. And it will surely come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive. They urge you to hasten the punishment. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers." Ad-Dahhak went to interpret this verse with a strange statement, so he said regarding his saying: The command of God has come meaning His obligations and limits. Ibn Jarir rejected him and said: We do not know of anyone who hastened the obligations and laws before their existence, unlike the torment, for they hastened it before it was, out of rejection and denial. I said: As God Almighty said: "Those who do not believe in it hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute about the Hour are in extreme error." Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was reported on the authority of Yahya bin Adam, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah, the client of Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba, on the authority of Ka’b bin Alqamah, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Hujaira, on the authority of Uqba bin Amir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “At the Hour, a black cloud will rise upon you from the west like a shield, and it will continue to rise in the sky. Then a caller will call out in it: O people. The people will turn to one another: Did you hear? Some of them will say: Yes, and some of them will doubt. Then he will call out a second time: O people. The people will say to one another: Did you hear? They will say: Yes. Then he will call out a third time: O people, the command of God has come, so do not hasten it.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, two men will spread out a garment but will never fold it up, and a man will extend his cistern but will never water anything in it, and a man will milk his camel but will never drink it.” He said: And the people will be busy. Then God, the Most High, exalted Himself from their associating partners with Him. Other than Him and their worship of other idols and rivals with Him, He is exalted and sanctified, greatly exalted. These are the ones who deny the Hour, so He said: Glory be to Him and He is exalted above what they associate with Him.
16:2: The Almighty says: He sends down the angels with the Spirit meaning the revelation, as He says: "And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants" and His saying: On whomever He wills of His servants and they are the prophets, as the Almighty says: God knows best with whom to place His message and He says: God chooses from the angels messengers and from the people and He says: "He casts the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants to warn of the Day of Meeting * The Day when they will appear, nothing of them will be hidden from God. To whom belongs the dominion today? To God, the One, the Prevailing." And His saying: To warn meaning to warn that there is no god except Me, so fear Me meaning fear My punishment for whoever disobeys My command and worships other than Me.
16:3: The Almighty tells us about His creation of the upper world, which is the heavens, and the lower world, which is the earth and what it contains, and that this was created with truth, not for frivolity, but rather that He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good with goodness. Then He cleared Himself of the association of anyone who worships anyone other than Him, and He is the One who is independent in creation alone, with no partner for Him. For this reason, He deserves to be worshipped alone, with no partner for Him. Then He pointed out the creation of the human race from a drop of semen, i.e., a weak, insignificant drop. When He became independent and advanced, then He disputed with His Lord, the Almighty, and denied Him and fought His messengers. He was created to be a servant, not an opponent, as the Almighty said: "And it is He who created from water a human being and made him a relative by bloodline and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent. * And they worship besides God that which neither benefits them nor harms them. And ever is the disbeliever, against his Lord, a supporter." And His statement: “Has not man considered that We created him from a sperm-drop, then at once he is a clear adversary? And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, ‘Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?’ Say, ‘He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation.’” And in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Majah on the authority of Busr ibn Jahash, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spat into his hand, then said: “God Almighty says: Son of Adam, how can you outstrip Me when I created you from the like of this, until when I proportioned you and made you even, you walked between your two garments, and the earth was slow from you, so you gathered and withheld until, when you reached the throat, I said, ‘Shall I give charity?’ But when is the time for charity?”

16:5: God Almighty bestows His blessings upon His servants by creating for them livestock, which are camels, cows, and sheep, as He separated them in Surat Al-An'am into eight pairs, and by making for them benefits and interests from their wool, fur, and hair, which they wear and bedding themselves with, and from their milk they drink and eat from their children, and the beauty they have in them, which is adornment. For this reason He said: And for you there is beauty in them when you bring them back to pasture which is the time when they return in the evening from pasture, as they are the longest in their flanks, the largest in their udders, and the highest in their humps, and when you send them out to pasture meaning in the morning when you send them out to pasture, and they carry your loads which are the heavy loads that you are unable to transport and carry to a land which you could not have reached except with great difficulty and that is in Hajj, Umrah, conquest, trade, and what is similar to that, you use them in various uses such as riding and loading, like His saying: “And indeed for you in the livestock is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and for you therein are benefits.” And He shows you His signs. So which of the signs of God do you deny?” This is why He said here after enumerating these blessings: Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful. That is, your Lord is the One who provided for you these livestock and subjected them to you, as in His statement: Have they not seen that We have created for them from what Our hands have made livestock, so they own them? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat. And He said: “And He has made for you ships and livestock on which to ride, that you may mount on their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you mount on them and say, ‘Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have subdued it.’ And indeed, to our Lord we will return.” Ibn Abbas said: Therein is warmth for you, that is, clothing, and benefits, that is, what you benefit from of foods and drinks. Abdul Razzaq said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Warmth and benefits of the offspring of every animal. Mujahid said: For you therein is warmth, meaning woven clothing, and benefits of riding, meat, and milk. Qatada said: Warmth and benefits, meaning: For you therein is clothing, benefit, and a means of transportation. And more than one of the commentators said the same with similar wording.

16:8: This is another type of what the Blessed and Exalted created for His servants, with which He bestows His favor upon them, and they are horses, mules, and donkeys, which He made for riding and adornment, and that is the greatest purpose of them. And since He separated them from the livestock and singled them out for mention, those scholars who held that horse meat is forbidden based their argument on what they held regarding it, such as Imam Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, and those jurists who agreed with him, that the Almighty linked it to mules and donkeys, and they are forbidden, as was proven by the Prophetic Sunnah, and most scholars held this opinion. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir narrated: Ya`qub told me, Ibn `Ulayyah told us, Hisham al-Dastawa`i informed us, Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us, on the authority of the client of Nafi` ibn `Alqamah, that Ibn `Abbas disliked the meat of horses, mules and donkeys, and he used to say: God the Almighty said: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat. This is for eating. And horses, mules and donkeys that you may ride them. This is for riding. And it was also narrated by way of Sa`id ibn Jubayr and others on the authority of Ibn `Abbas in a similar manner. Al-Hakam ibn `Utaybah also said something similar, may God be pleased with him. They relied on a hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad: Yazid ibn `Abd Rabbih told us, Baqiyah ibn al-Waleed told us, Thawr ibn Yazid told us, on the authority of Salih ibn Yahya ibn al-Muqaddam ibn Ma`dikarib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Khalid ibn al-Waleed, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade eating the meat of horses, mules and donkeys. It was narrated by Abu Dawood, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah on the authority of Salih bin Yahya bin Al-Muqaddam, and there is some discussion about it. Ahmad also narrated it from another chain of transmission, more simply and clearly, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik told us, Muhammad ibn Harb told us, Sulayman ibn Salim told us, on the authority of Salih ibn Yahya ibn al-Muqaddam, on the authority of his grandfather al-Muqaddam ibn Ma’dikarib, who said: We went on a summer expedition with Khalid ibn al-Walid, and our companions were hungry for meat, so they asked me for a piece of meat, so I gave it to them, and they tied it up, and I said: Stay where you are until I go to Khalid and ask him, so I went to him and asked him, and he said: We went on a campaign with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Khaybar, and the people rushed into the pens of the Jews, so he ordered me to call for the congregational prayer, and no one will enter Paradise except a Muslim, then he said: “O people, you have rushed into the pens of the Jews. Beware, the property of those with whom a treaty has been made is not permissible except by right, and the meat of domesticated donkeys, horses, and mules is forbidden to you, and every fanged beast of prey, and every taloned bird.” The piece of meat is the room, and his saying they tied it up means they tied it up with a rope to slaughter it, and the pens and orchards are close to the cities, and it is as if this The deed occurred after they were given the covenant and treated half of it, and God knows best. If this hadith were authentic, it would be a text prohibiting horse meat, but it cannot be resisted by what was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the meat of domesticated donkeys, and permitted the meat of horses. Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated it with two chains of narration, each of which met the conditions of Muslim, on the authority of Jabir, who said: On the day of Khaybar, we slaughtered horses, mules, and donkeys. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade us from mules and donkeys, but he did not forbid us from horses. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Asma bint Abi Bakr may God be pleased with them both, she said: We slaughtered a horse during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and ate it while we were in Madinah. This is more indicative, stronger, and more established. The majority of scholars, including Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad, their companions, and most of the early and later generations, agreed with this view. And God knows best. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Mulaykah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Horses were wild, then God tamed them for Ishmael, son of Abraham (peace be upon them both). Wahb ibn Munabbih mentioned in his Isra’iliyyat that God created horses from the south wind, and God knows best. The text indicates the permissibility of riding these beasts, including mules. A mule was given as a gift to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he used to ride it, although he had forbidden donkeys to mate with horses lest the lineage be cut off. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Ubaid told me, Umar from the family of Hudhayfah told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Dihya Al-Kalbi, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, should I not mount a donkey on a horse for you so that it may produce a mule for you to ride? He said: Only those who do not know do that.
16:9: When the Almighty mentioned animals that are easy to follow in physical ways, He pointed out the spiritual and religious ways. The Qur’an often transitions from physical matters to spiritual and religious matters that are beneficial, such as His Almighty saying: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is righteousness. And He Almighty said: “O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and adornment. But the clothing of righteousness - that is best.” And when the Almighty mentioned in this Surah the animals of livestock and others that they ride and on which they achieve a need in their hearts, and carry their loads to distant countries and places and difficult journeys, He began to mention the paths that people take to Him, so He explained that the truth among them is that which leads to Him, so He said: And upon God is the determination of the path, such as His saying: And that this is My path, which is straight, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path. And He said: “He said: This is My path, which is straight.” Mujahid said about His statement, And upon God is the direction of the way, he said: The path of truth is upon God. Al-Suddi said, And upon God is the direction of the way, Islam. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, And upon God is the direction of the way, he said: And upon God is the explanation, meaning He explains guidance and misguidance. And this is what Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated on his authority, and this is what Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said. And the statement of Mujahid here is stronger in terms of context, because the Almighty informed us that there are paths that lead to Him, and none of them leads to Him except the path of truth, which is the path that He has legislated and approved of, and everything other than it is blocked and deeds done in it are rejected. For this reason the Almighty said, And among them are those that are deviant, meaning those that deviate, inclined, and stray from the truth. Ibn Abbas and others said: They are the different paths, opinions and scattered desires such as Judaism, Christianity and Zoroastrianism. Ibn Masoud read: And among them is one who is unjust. Then God Almighty informed us that all of that is due to His power and will, so He said: And if He had willed, He could have guided you all. Just as God Almighty said: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together. And He said: “And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ. Except whom your Lord has given mercy. And for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: ‘I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.’”
16:10: When God the Almighty mentioned the blessings He bestowed upon them of livestock and beasts, He proceeded to mention His blessings upon them in sending down rain from the sky, which is the elevation of what they have in it as a means of provision and enjoyment for them and their livestock. He said: From it you have a drink, meaning He made it sweet and pure, making it permissible for you to drink it, and He did not make it salty and bitter. And from it are trees in which you graze your livestock. That is, He brought forth for you from it trees in which you graze your livestock. As Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said in His statement in which you graze, meaning you graze, and from it are the grazing camels, and saum means grazing. Ibn Majah narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade saum before sunrise. And His statement: He causes to grow for you thereby crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and from all kinds of fruits, meaning He brings them out of the earth with this single water, with their different kinds, tastes, colors, scents, and shapes. For this reason He said: Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought, meaning an indication and proof that there is no god but God, as God Almighty said: “Is He who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you from the sky water, and We caused to grow thereby gardens of delight? It was not for you to make their trees grow. Is there a god with God? Rather, they are a people who equate others with Him.” Then God Almighty said:

16:12: The Almighty reminds His servants of His great signs and immense favors in His subjection of the night and day to alternate, the sun and moon to revolve, and the fixed and moving stars in the regions of the heavens as light and radiance to guide people in the darkness, and each of them moves in its orbit in which God Almighty has placed it, moving with a determined movement that does not increase or decrease from it, and all are under His control and authority and His subjection and His estimation and facilitation, as in His saying: “Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself on the Throne. He covers the night with the day, pursuing it rapidly. And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds.” For this reason He said: Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason. That is, indications of the Almighty’s dazzling power and His great authority for a people who reason about God and understand His proofs. And His statement: And what He has created for you on the earth of varying colours When God Almighty called attention to the features of the heavens, He called attention to what He created on the earth of wondrous matters, and the various things of animals, minerals, plants and inanimate objects in their different colours and shapes, and what they contain of benefits and properties. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember meaning the favours and blessings of God, so they are thankful for them.

16:14: The Almighty tells us about His subjugation of the turbulent sea, and He bestows His favor upon His servants by making it easy for them to ride it, and by making fish and whales in it, and making their meat permissible for His servants, whether alive or dead, in the state of ihram or in the state of ihram, and what He creates in it of pearls and precious jewels, and making it easy for His servants to extract from its depths an ornament that they wear, and His subjugation of the sea to carry the ships that plow it, or it was said that the winds plow it, and both are correct, and it was said that they plow it with their protrusions, which are their humped fronts - which He guided the servants to make and guided them to that as an inheritance from their father Noah, peace be upon him, for he was the first to ride ships, and he was the one who taught them how to make them, then the people took it from him century after century, and generation after generation, traveling from one country to another, and from one region to another, to bring what is there to what is here, and what is here to what is there, and for this reason the Almighty said: "And that you may seek of His bounty And perhaps you will be grateful for His blessings and kindness. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: I found in my book on the authority of Muhammad bin Muawiyah Al-Baghdadi, he said: Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Amr told us on the authority of Sahl bin Abi Saleh on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: God spoke to the western sea and spoke to the eastern sea, and said to the western sea: I am carrying in you some of my servants, so what will you do with them? It said: I will drown them. It said: Your strength is in your regions, and I will carry them on my hand, and I have forbidden adornment and hunting. And He spoke to this eastern sea and said: I am carrying in you some of my servants, so what will you do with them? It said: I will carry them on my hand, and I will be to them like a mother to her child. So He rewarded it with adornment and hunting. Then Al-Bazzar said: We do not know of anyone who narrated it on the authority of Sahl other than Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Amr, and he is a fabricator of hadith. Sahl narrated it on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Abi Ayyash on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Then God mentioned the earth and what He cast into it of lofty mountains and firm mountains, so that the earth would be stable and not shake, that is, it would shake with the animals on it so that their life would not be pleasant because of that. For this reason, He said: And the mountains He has fixed firmly. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of Qatada, I heard al-Hasan say: When the earth was created, it was shaking, so they said: This is not stable on its back for anyone. So they woke up and the mountains had been created, and the angels did not know from what the mountains were created. And Saeed said on the authority of Qatada on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of Qays ibn Ubadah that when God created the earth, it began to shake, so the angels said: This is not stable on its back for anyone. So it woke up in the morning and it had its firm mountains. And Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj ibn Munhal told me, Hammad told us on the authority of Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: When God created the earth, it shivered and said: O Lord, do You make the children of Adam commit sins and make me commit wickedness? He said: So God established in it mountains that you see and that you do not see, and its stability was like shaking flesh. And His saying: And rivers and paths means that He made therein rivers that flow from one place to another as a provision for the servants, springing up in one place and being a provision for the people of another place, so it cuts through the plains, wildernesses and wastelands, and penetrates the mountains and hills, until it reaches the land that He has made subservient to its people, and it moves on the earth right and left, south and north, east and west, between small and large, and valleys that flow sometimes and stop at other times, and between a spring and a gathering, and the strength of the movement and its slowness is according to what He willed and decreed and made subservient and easy, for there is no god but Him and no lord but Him, and likewise He made therein paths, meaning roads that are taken from one country to another, so that the Most High even cuts through the mountain until what is between them is a passage and a path, as the Most High said: And We have made therein paths as paths Al-An’am 2:17. His saying: And signs means indications of large mountains, small hills, and the like, by which travelers by land and sea can find their way if they lose their way. And his saying: And by the stars they are guided meaning in the darkness of the night, Ibn Abbas said, and from Malik in his saying: And signs and by the stars they are guided he says: the stars and they are the mountains, then the Almighty pointed out His greatness and that worship is only due to Him and not to other than Him of the idols that do not create anything but are created, and for this reason He said: Is He who creates like he who does not create? Will you not remember? Then He pointed out to them the abundance of His blessings upon them and His kindness to them, so He said: “And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful” meaning He overlooks you, and if He asked you to thank for all of His blessings you would be unable to do that, and if He ordered you to do so you would weaken and abandon it, and if He punished you He would punish you and He is not unjust to you, but He is Forgiving and Merciful, He forgives much and rewards for little, and Ibn Jarir said: He says that God is Forgiving of what was from you of shortcomings in thanking for some of that if you repent and return to His obedience and following His pleasure, Merciful to you and will not punish you after that Repentance and repentance.

16:19: The Almighty informs us that He knows the innermost thoughts and secrets as He knows the outward appearances, and He will reward every worker for his deeds on the Day of Resurrection, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. Then He informs us that the idols that they call upon instead of God do not create anything, and they are created, as Al-Khalil said: Do you worship what you carve? * And God created you and what you do. And His statement: Dead, not alive means that they are inanimate objects with no souls in them, so they do not hear, see, or understand. And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected means that they do not know when the Hour will be, so how can any benefit, reward, or recompense be hoped for in this case? This is only hoped for from the One who knows everything and is the Creator of everything.

16:22: The Almighty informs that there is no god but the One, the Unique, the Self-Sufficient, and He informs that the hearts of the disbelievers deny that, as He informs about them being amazed by that: Have you made the gods one god? Indeed, this is a strange thing. And the Almighty says: “And when God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter are filled with disgust. But when those other than Him are mentioned, at once they rejoice.” And His statement: while they are arrogant means about worshipping God while their hearts deny His Oneness, as He said: Indeed, those who are arrogant about My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible. And for this reason He said here: There is no doubt meaning truly that God knows what they conceal and what they declare meaning He will reward them for that with the most complete reward Indeed, He does not love the arrogant.

16:24: God the Almighty says: And when it is said to these deniers, What has your Lord revealed? they say, turning away from the answer, Legends of the ancients. That is, He did not reveal anything. Rather, what is recited to us are legends of the ancients, that is, taken from the books of the predecessors, as God the Almighty said: And they say, 'Legends of the ancients which he wrote down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening.' That is, they fabricate against the Messenger and say contradictory and different statements, all of which are false, as God the Almighty said: See how they strike for you examples, then they have gone astray and cannot find a way. That is because everyone who deviated from the truth, whatever he said, made a mistake. They used to say: a magician, a poet, a soothsayer, and a madman. Then their matter settled on what their only sheikh, called Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi, invented for them when he "thought and calculated * Then he killed how he calculated * Then he killed how he calculated * Then he looked * Then he frowned and frowned * Then he turned away and was arrogant * And he said, 'This is nothing but magic that is transmitted and narrated.'" That is, they dispersed from his words and opinion. May God curse them. God the Almighty said: That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge. That is, We only decreed that they should say that so that they may bear their own burdens and some of the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge, meaning that the sin of their misguidance in themselves and the sin of their misleading others and their following them would be upon them, as came in the hadith: “Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like that of those who follow him, without diminishing anything from their reward. And whoever calls to misguidance will have a sin like that of those who follow him, without diminishing anything from their sins.” And God the Almighty said: And they will surely bear their own burdens and other burdens with their own burdens, and they will be asked on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent. And thus Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge, that it is like His saying: And they will surely bear their own burdens and other burdens with their own burdens. And Mujahid said: They will bear their own burdens, their sins and the sins of those who obeyed them, and it will not be lightened. There is no punishment for those who obey them.

Their faces will be blackened meaning because of their lies and fabrications. No evil will touch them meaning on the Day of Resurrection nor will they grieve meaning the greatest terror will not grieve them, rather they will be safe from every terror, removed from every evil, attaining every good.
16:26: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Those before them plotted, he said: It is Nimrod who built the tower. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. And Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam: The first tyrant on earth was Nimrod, so God sent a mosquito upon him and it entered his nostril, so he remained for four hundred years hitting his head with hammers, and the most merciful of people to him was the one who gathered his hands and hit his head with them, and he was a tyrant for four hundred years, so God punished him for four hundred years as his kingdom was, then he killed him, and he is the one who built the tower to the sky about which God Almighty said: So God destroyed their building from the foundations. And others said: Rather, it was Bukhtanasr, and they mentioned the plot that God narrated here as He said in Surat Ibrahim 14:And if their plot was such that mountains would move from it. And others said: This is a parable to invalidate what those who disbelieved in God and associated others with Him in worship did, as Noah, peace be upon him, said: And they plotted a great plot, meaning they conspired to mislead people by every trick and inclined them to their polytheism by every means, as their followers will say to them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Rather, their plot was by night and by day when you commanded us to We disbelieve in God and attribute to Him equals. And His saying: So God came upon their building from the foundations means He uprooted it from its roots and nullified their work, like the saying of God the Most High: Every time they kindled a fire for war, God extinguished it and His saying: “So God came upon them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, O you who have insight.” And God said here: “So God came upon their building from the foundations, and the roof fell upon them from above them, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive. Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them” meaning He will reveal their scandals and what their consciences concealed, and He will make it public, like the saying of God the Most High: The Day when secrets will be exposed meaning they will appear and become famous, as in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A banner will be raised for every traitor on the Day of Resurrection at his backside according to the extent of his treachery, and it will be said, ‘This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.’” And thus the people will see what they concealed of deceit and God will disgrace them in front of all creation, and the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, will say to them: He knocked at them and rebuked them, Where are My partners for whom you used to quarrel? You used to fight and be hostile for their sake. Where are they when it comes to your victory and salvation here? Will they help you or will they be victorious? “For he has no power nor helper.” So when the argument is directed at them and the evidence is established against them, and the word is justified against them and they remain silent about apologizing when there is no escape, Those who were given knowledge will say, and they are the masters in this world and the hereafter, and the informants of the truth in this world and the hereafter, then they will say at that time, Indeed, disgrace and evil will be upon the disbelievers today. That is, disgrace and punishment will surround today whoever disbelieved in God and associated with Him that which neither harms nor benefits him.

16:28: The Almighty tells about the state of the unjust polytheists themselves when they are dying and the angels come to them to seize their evil souls. “So throw down your peace,” that is, show hearing, obedience, and submission, saying, We did not do any evil, as they will say on the Day of Resurrection. By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists. “On the Day when God will resurrect them all, they will swear to Him as they swear to you,” God said, belying them in their saying that. “Yes, God is Knowing of what you used to do. So enter the gates of Hell to abide therein. 16:33: God the Almighty says, threatening the polytheists for their persistence in falsehood and their deception with the world: Do these people expect anything but the angels to come to them to take their souls? Qatada said, or the command of your Lord comes meaning the Day of Resurrection and the horrors they will witness. And His statement: Thus did those before them meaning thus did their predecessors, their peers, and those like them among the polytheists persist in their polytheism until they tasted the wrath of God and were subjected to what they are in of torment and punishment. And God did not wrong them because God the Almighty excused them and established His proofs against them by sending His messengers and revealing His books. But they were wronging themselves meaning by disobeying the messengers and denying what they brought, so this is why God's punishment befell them for that. And that which they used to mock encompassed them meaning it surrounded them with painful torment. That which they used to mock meaning they mocked the messengers when they threatened them with God's punishment. So this is why it will be said to them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:This is the Fire which you used to deny.

16:35: The Almighty tells about the deception of the polytheists in what they are in of polytheism and their excuse, arguing with predestination by saying: If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything besides Him meaning of the lakes, the free-ranging waters, the means, and other things that they had innovated and invented of their own accord, for which He had not sent down any authority. The gist of their words is that if the Almighty had been averse to what we did, He would have denounced it to us with punishment, and He would not have enabled us to do it. God the Almighty said, responding to their doubt: Is there anything upon the messengers except the clear notification? meaning that the matter is not as you claim, that He did not denounce it to you, rather He denounced it to you with the strongest denial, and He forbade you from it with the most emphatic prohibition, and He sent to every nation, meaning in every century and group, a messenger, and all of them call to the worship of God and forbid the worship of anything other than Him, Worship God and avoid the false gods. So the Almighty has not ceased sending messengers to the people with that since it happened. Polytheism among the children of Adam, among the people of Noah, to whom Noah was sent, and he was the first messenger sent by God to the people of the earth until he sealed them with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, whose call was applied to mankind and jinn in the East and the West, and all of them are as God Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no god except Me, so worship Me.’ And God Almighty said: And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers, ‘Did We appoint other gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?’ And God Almighty said in this noble verse: And We have certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities.’ So how can it be permissible for any of the polytheists after this to say, If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him? His legal will for them is negated, because He forbade them from that on the tongues of His messengers. As for His cosmic will, which is enabling them to do that in a certain measure, they have no proof in it, because God Almighty created Hell and its people from the devils and disbelievers, and He is not pleased for His servants to disbelieve, and He has the right to do so. A strong argument and decisive wisdom. Then the Almighty informed us that He condemned them with punishment in this world after warning the messengers, so He said: “And among them were those whom God guided, and among them were those upon whom error was due. So travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied.” That is, ask about what happened to those who disobeyed the messengers and denied the truth, how God destroyed them, and for the disbelievers there is the like thereof. So He said: And those before them denied, so how was My denunciation? Then God the Almighty informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that his eagerness to guide them would not benefit them if God wanted to misguide them, as He the Almighty said: And he whom God intends to test, you will not possess for him anything from God. And Noah said to his al-Nas 114:And my advice will not benefit you, if I want to advise you, if God wants to misguide you. And He said in this noble verse: If you are eager to guide them, then indeed God guides not he whom He misguides. As God the Almighty said: He whom God misguides - there is no guide for him, and He leaves them wandering blindly in their transgression. And He the Almighty said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them until they see the painful punishment. And His statement: Then indeed God means His affair and command is that whatever He wills happens and whatever He does not will does not happen. For this reason He said: He does not guide he whom He misguides, meaning whoever He misguides. So who is there who can guide him after God? That is, no one. And they have no helpers, that is, who can save them from His punishment and His bonds. “Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds.”

16:38: The Almighty says, informing about the polytheists, that they swore by God with their strongest oaths, meaning they strove hard in swearing, and they made strong oaths that God will not resurrect those who die, meaning they ruled that out, and they denied the messengers when they informed them of that and swore the opposite. So the Almighty said, denying them and responding to them, Yes, meaning yes, that will be a promise binding upon Him, meaning it is inevitable, but most people do not know, meaning because of their ignorance they disobey the messengers and fall into disbelief. Then the Almighty mentioned His wisdom in the Resurrection and the resurrection of bodies on the Day of Calling, saying, To make clear to them, meaning to the people, that over which they differ, meaning of everything, that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did and recompense those who did good with goodness, “and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars,” meaning in their oaths and oaths that God will not resurrect those who die, and for this reason they will be called on the Day of Resurrection to the fire of Hell, and the guards will say to them, This is the fire in which you were. Then the Almighty informed about His ability to do whatever He wills, and that nothing on earth or in heaven is beyond His power. Rather, His command, when He wills something, is to say to it, Be, and it is. The Resurrection is like that: when He wills it to be, He only commands it once, and it is as He wills, as in His saying: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. And He said: Your creation and your resurrection are not but as a single soul. And He said in this noble verse: Our command to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, “Be, and it is.” That is, that We command it once, and then it is, as the poet said: If God wants something, He just says to it, Be, and it is. That is, He, the Most High, does not need confirmation in what He commands, for He, the Most High, does not prevent or oppose, because He is the One, the Subduer, the Great, whose authority, power, and might have subdued everything. There is no god but Him, and there is no lord but Him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabah mentioned, Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ata’ told me that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: God, the Most High, said: The son of Adam cursed Me, and it was not right for him to do so, and the son of Adam lied to Me, and it was not right for him to do so. As for his lying to Me, He said: And they swear by God their most solemn oaths that God will not raise up anyone who dies. He said: And I said: Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him, but most people do not know. As for his cursing Me, He said: God is the third of three. I said: “Say: He is God, the One. God, the Self-Sufficient. He does not beget, nor was He begotten. And there is none comparable to Him.” This is how he mentioned it, with a chain of transmission ending with the Prophet, and it is in the two Sahihs with a chain of transmission ending with the Prophet, with a different wording.

16:40: The Almighty says, informing about the polytheists, that they swore by God with their strongest oaths, meaning they strove hard in swearing, and they made strong oaths that God will not resurrect those who die, meaning they ruled that out, and they denied the messengers when they informed them of that and swore the opposite. So the Almighty said, denying them and responding to them, Yes, meaning yes, that will be a promise binding upon Him, meaning it is inevitable, but most people do not know, meaning because of their ignorance they disobey the messengers and fall into disbelief. Then the Almighty mentioned His wisdom in the Resurrection and the resurrection of bodies on the Day of Calling, saying, To make clear to them, meaning to the people, that over which they differ, meaning of everything, that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did and recompense those who did good with goodness, “and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars,” meaning in their oaths and oaths that God will not resurrect those who die, and for this reason they will be called on the Day of Resurrection to the fire of Hell, and the guards will say to them, This is the fire in which you were. Then the Almighty informed about His ability to do whatever He wills, and that nothing on earth or in heaven is beyond His power. Rather, His command, when He wills something, is to say to it, Be, and it is. The Resurrection is like that: when He wills it to be, He only commands it once, and it is as He wills, as in His saying: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. And He said: Your creation and your resurrection are not but as a single soul. And He said in this noble verse: Our command to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, “Be, and it is.” That is, that We command it once, and then it is, as the poet said: If God wants something, He just says to it, Be, and it is. That is, He, the Most High, does not need confirmation in what He commands, for He, the Most High, does not prevent or oppose, because He is the One, the Subduer, the Great, whose authority, power, and might have subdued everything. There is no god but Him, and there is no lord but Him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabah mentioned, Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ata’ told me that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: God, the Most High, said: The son of Adam cursed Me, and it was not right for him to do so, and the son of Adam lied to Me, and it was not right for him to do so. As for his lying to Me, He said: And they swear by God their most solemn oaths that God will not raise up anyone who dies. He said: And I said: Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him, but most people do not know. As for his cursing Me, He said: God is the third of three. I said: “Say: He is God, the One. God, the Self-Sufficient. He does not beget, nor was He begotten. And there is none comparable to Him.” This is how he mentioned it, with a chain of transmission ending with the Prophet, and it is in the two Sahihs with a chain of transmission ending with the Prophet, with a different wording.
16:41: God Almighty tells us about His reward for the emigrants in His path seeking His pleasure, who left their homes, brothers and friends hoping for God’s reward and recompense. It is possible that the reason for its revelation was about the emigrants from Abyssinia, whose people’s harm to them in Mecca intensified until they left them and went to the land of Abyssinia so that they could worship their Lord. Among their nobles were Uthman ibn Affan, with his wife Ruqayyah, daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ja’far ibn Abi Talib, cousin of the Messenger, and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Aswad, in a group of nearly eighty men and women, male and female, may God be pleased with them and satisfy them. And He did so, so God Almighty promised them a good reward in this world and the hereafter, saying: We will surely give them a good settlement in this world. Ibn Abbas, al-Sha’bi and Qatadah said: Medina. It was said: Good provision, as Mujahid said. There is no contradiction between the two statements, for they left their homes and wealth, so God compensated them with something better in this world. For whoever leaves something for God God compensated him with something better for him than him, and so it happened, for God empowered them in the land, and made them rule over the necks of the servants, and they became princes and rulers, and each of them was an imam for the righteous, and He informed that His reward for the emigrants in the Hereafter is greater than what He gave them in this world, so He said: And the reward of the Hereafter is greater meaning than what We gave them in this world, if they only knew meaning if those who stayed behind from emigration with them knew what God had stored for those who obeyed Him and followed His Messenger, and for this Hisham said on the authority of Al-Awam on the authority of someone who told him that Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, when he gave a man from the emigrants his gift, he would say: Take it, may God bless you in it, this is what God promised you in this world, and what He has stored for you in the Hereafter is better, then he recited this verse: We will surely give them a good settlement in this world, and the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew. Then God Almighty described them, saying: Those who are patient and put their trust in their Lord. That is, they were patient in the face of harm from their people, putting their trust in God, who gave them a good outcome in this world and the hereafter.

16:43: Ad-Dahhak said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: When God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a Messenger, the Arabs, or those who denied it among them, denied it and said: God is greater than for His Messenger to be a human being. So He revealed: Is it a wonder to people that We have inspired a man from among them, ‘Warn the people?’ The verse, and He said: “And We did not send before you except men to whom We inspired. So ask the people of the message if you do not know.” Meaning the people of the previous books. Were the messengers to them human beings or angels? If they were angels, you would deny it, and if they were human, do not deny that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a messenger. God Almighty said: And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns. They are not from the people of heaven as you said. Likewise, it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas that what is meant by the people of remembrance are the people of the Book. Mujahid and Al-A’mash said the same. The statement of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd: Remembrance is the Qur’an, and he cited as evidence his statement: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Remembrance and indeed, We will be its guardian, is correct, but it is not what is meant here, because the opponent does not return to confirming it after denying it. Likewise, the statement of Abu Ja’far al-Baqir: We are the people of remembrance, and his meaning is that this nation is the people of remembrance, is correct, because this nation is more knowledgeable than all previous nations. The scholars of the Household of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon them, are among the best scholars if they are on the straight path, such as Ali and Ibn Abbas, and Ali’s sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and Muhammad Ibn al-Hanafiyyah and Ali Ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin, and Ali Ibn Abdullah Ibn Abbas, and Abu Ja’far al-Baqir, who is Muhammad Ibn Ali Ibn al-Husayn and his son Ja’far, and their likes and counterparts and their forms, who hold fast to the strong rope of God and His straight path, and recognize every rightful person’s right and descend to every position that God and His Messenger gave him and the hearts of His believing servants agreed upon. The point is that this noble verse informed that the messengers who came before Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, were human beings just as he was human, as God Almighty said: Say, ‘Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?’ And nothing prevented people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, ‘Has God sent a human messenger?’ And God Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And God Almighty said: And We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, nor were they immortal. And He said: Say, ‘I am not an innovation.’ From the Messengers” and God Almighty said: “Say, ‘I am only a human being like you, to whom is revealed. ’” Then God Almighty guided those who doubted that the Messengers were human beings to ask the people of the previous books about the prophets who came before them, were their prophets human beings or angels? Then God Almighty mentioned that He sent them with clear proofs, meaning with arguments and evidence, and the Psalms, which are the books. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and others. The Psalms are the plural of Zabur. The Arabs say: Zabart Al-Kitab if you wrote it. God Almighty said: And everything they did was in the Psalms, and He said: And We had already written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants. Then God Almighty said: And We have sent down to you the Reminder, meaning the Qur’an, that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them, meaning from their Lord, because of your knowledge of the meaning of what God revealed and your keenness on it and your following of it, and because of our knowledge that you are the best of creation and the master of the children of Adam, so you explain to them what is most beautiful and explain to them what is unclear, and perhaps they will reflect, meaning they will look at themselves and be guided and win salvation in both abodes.

16:45: The Almighty tells us about His forbearance and His giving respite to the disobedient who commit evil deeds and call for them, and plot against people in calling them and urging them to do them, while He is able to cause the earth to swallow them up or bring punishment to them from where they do not perceive, meaning from where they do not know it will come to them, as in the Almighty’s saying: “Do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you up, and then it will sway? Or do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven that He will not send upon you a hurricane? Then you will know how [a warner] is.” And His saying: Or He will seize them in their turning over, meaning in their turning over in their livelihoods and their preoccupation with them in their travels and other distracting occupations. Qatada and Al-Suddi said: Their turning over means their travels. Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: In their turning over at night and during the day, as in His saying: “Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come to them at night while they are asleep? Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come to them at noon while they are playing?” And His statement: They will not be able to frustrate God means they will not frustrate God in any condition they are in. And His statement: Or He seizes them while they are fearful of Him seizing them means that God seizes them while they are fearful of Him seizing them, for that would be more eloquent and severe, for what is expected with fear is severe. For this reason, Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or He seizes them while they are fearful means: If you wish, He seizes him after the death of his companion and his fear of that. And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and others. Then God the Almighty said: Then your Lord is Kind and Merciful meaning since He does not hasten to punish you, as is proven in the two Sahihs: "No one is more patient with the harm he hears than God. They attribute to Him a son, while He provides for them and cures them." And in them: Indeed, God grants respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited: "And such is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe." And God the Almighty said: And how many a town was I granted respite while it was doing wrong? Then I seized it, and to Me is the final destination.

16:48: The Almighty tells us about His greatness, majesty and pride to which everything has submitted, and to which all things and creatures have submitted: inanimate objects and animals, and those charged with them from among mankind and jinn, and the angels. He informed us that everything that has a shadow that takes shade to the right and to the left, that is, morning and evening, is prostrating in its shadow to God the Almighty. Mujahid said: When the sun sets, everything prostrates to God the Almighty, and so did Qatada, Ad-Dahhak and others. His statement, and they are humbled means submissive. Mujahid also said: The prostration of everything is its shade, and he mentioned the mountains, saying: Their prostration is their shade. Abu Ghalib Ash-Shaibani said: The waves of the sea are His prayer, and He placed them in the position of those who have reason, since He attributed prostration to them, saying: And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures as He said: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows in the mornings and the evenings. And His statement: And the angels, and they are not arrogant, meaning they prostrate to God, meaning they are not arrogant about worshipping Him. They fear their Lord above them, meaning they prostrate in fear and awe of the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted. And they do what they are commanded, meaning they persevere in obeying Him, the Most High, and complying with His commands, and abandoning His prohibitions.

16:51: The Almighty informs us that there is no god but Him, and that none should be worshipped except Him alone, with no partner for Him, for He is the Owner of everything, its Creator and its Lord. And to Him belongs the religion, always. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Maymun ibn Mihran, As-Suddi, Qatadah and more than one said: That is, always. And from Ibn Abbas also: That is, obligatory. Mujahid said: That is, sincerely for Him, that is, to Him alone is the worship of those in the heavens and the earth, like His statement: Do they seek other than the religion of God while to Him have submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned? This is according to the statement of Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah, so it is from the category of report. As for the statement of Mujahid, it is from the category of request, that is, fear that you associate anything with Me and be sincere in obedience to Me, like His statement, the Most High: Unquestionably, to God belongs the pure religion. Then He informed that He is the Owner of benefit and harm, and that whatever provision, blessing, well-being, and victory the servants have is from His grace and kindness to them. Then when harm befalls you, to Him you cry for help. That is, because you know that no one is able to remove it except Him, so when necessities arise, you turn to Him and ask Him and insist in desiring Him, seeking His help, like His statement, the Most High: “And when harm befalls you at sea, lost are those you call upon except Him. But when He brings you safe to land, you turn away, and ever is man ungrateful.” And He said here: Then when it is removed. It was said: The lam here is the lam of consequence. It was also said: The lam of justification means that We decreed that for them so that they would disbelieve, that is, conceal and deny the blessings of God upon them and that He is the One who bestowed blessings upon them, the One who removed punishments from them. Then He threatened them, saying, Then enjoy yourselves, that is, do whatever you want and enjoy what you are in for a little while. You will soon know, that is, the consequences of that.

16:56: The Almighty tells about the ugliness of the polytheists who worshipped other than Him, idols, statues, and rivals, without knowledge, and “And they attributed to God a portion of what He created of crops and livestock, and said, ‘This is for God,’ according to their claim, and ‘This is for our partners.’ So whatever was for their partners does not reach God, and whatever was for God, it reaches their partners. So God the Almighty swore by His noble self that He would question them about that which they invented and fabricated, and that He would confront them for it, and that He would recompense them with the greatest recompense in the fire of Hell. So He said, By God, you will be asked about what you used to invent. Then the Almighty informed about them that they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females, and made them daughters of God, so they worshipped them with Him. That is indeed an unfair division. And His saying here: And they attribute daughters to God - glory be to Him means about their saying and their falsehood. “Behold, they say, out of their falsehood, ‘God has begotten a son,’ and they are liars. ‘He has chosen daughters over sons.’ What is the matter with you? How do you judge?” And His saying: And they will have whatever they desire means they choose for themselves males and are disgusted for themselves from the daughters which they attribute to God. God is far above what they say, for when one of them is given the report of a female, his face darkens meaning gloomy from worry and he is filled with inward grief silent from the intensity of his grief, he hides himself from the people meaning he hates for people to see him “because of the evil of the report he has been given.
