16:61: God the Almighty tells us about His forbearance with His creation despite their injustice, and that if He were to punish them for what they earned, He would not leave a single creature on the face of the earth, meaning He would destroy all the creatures of the earth following the destruction of the children of Adam. However, the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, is forbearing and conceals, and looks to a specified term, meaning He does not hasten to punish them, because if He did that to them, He would not have left anyone alive. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas that he said: The dung beetle was almost punished for the sin of the children of Adam, and he recited the verse: And if God were to punish people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave on the face of the earth a single creature. And likewise al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Ubaidah that he said: Abdullah said: The dung beetle was almost destroyed in its hole because of the sin of the children of Adam. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, Ismail ibn Hakim al-Khuza’i told us, Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Hanafi told us on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer on the authority of Abu Salamah who said: Abu Hurairah heard a man saying: The oppressor harms no one but himself. He said: So he turned to him and said: Yes, by God, even the houbara bustard dies in its nest because of the oppression of the oppressor. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Al-Walid bin Abdul-Malik told us, Ubaid God bin Sharhabil told us, Sulayman bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Muslima bin Abdullah, on the authority of his uncle Abu Mushajia bin Rabi’a, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were mentioned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “God does not delay anything when its time has come. Rather, the increase in life is through righteous offspring whom God grants to the servant, so they pray for him after him, and their prayers reach him in his grave. That is the increase in life.” His saying: And they attribute to God what they hate, meaning daughters and partners who are His slaves, and they are disgusted that one of them should have a partner in his wealth. And His statement: And their tongues describe falsehood that they will have the best is a denial of their claim that they will have the best in this world, and that if there is a return, then there is also the best for them, and a report of what was said by some of them, like His statement: “And if We let a man taste mercy from Us and then take it away from him, he is indeed despairing and ungrateful. And if We let him taste favor after an adversity has touched him, he will surely say, “Bad times have departed from me.” Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.” And His statement: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after an adversity has touched him, he will surely say, “This is for me, and I do not think the Hour will occur. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have with Him the best.” So We will surely inform those who disbelieve of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment. And His statement: Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, ‘I will surely be given wealth and children?’ And he said, reporting on one of the two men, that “he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself. He said, ‘I do not think that this will ever perish. And I do not think that the Hour will occur. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a return.’” So these people combined evil deeds with a false hope that they would be rewarded for that with good, and this is impossible, as Ibn Ishaq mentioned that a stone was found in the foundation of the Kaaba when they demolished it in order to renew it, on which were written rulings and sermons, including: Do you know the evil deeds and count the good deeds? Yes, just as grapes are picked from thorns. Mujahid and Qatadah said: And their tongues describe falsely that they will have the best meaning the young boys. Ibn Jarir said: They will have the best meaning the Day of Resurrection, as we have explained previously, and this is correct, praise be to God. That is why God the Almighty said in response to their wishing for that: There is no doubt meaning a truth that is inevitable that they will have the Fire meaning the Day of Resurrection and that they will be negligent. Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and others said: They will be forgotten and neglectful in it. This is like the statement of God the Almighty: So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs. Qatadah also said: Negligent means they will be hastened to the Fire from the word fart, which means the first to be received. There is no contradiction because they will be hastened to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and they will be forgotten in it, meaning they will remain eternally.

Ibn Jarir said: They will have the best meaning the Day of Resurrection, as we have explained previously, and this is correct, praise be to God. That is why God the Almighty said in response to their wishing for that: There is no doubt meaning a truth that is inevitable that they will have the Fire meaning the Day of Resurrection and that they will be negligent. Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and others said: They will be forgotten and neglectful in it. This is like the statement of God the Almighty: So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs. Qatadah also said: Negligent means they will be hastened to the Fire from the word fart, which means the first to be received. There is no contradiction because they will be hastened to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and they will be forgotten in it, meaning they will remain eternally.
16:63: God the Almighty mentions that He sent messengers to the past nations, but they denied the messengers. So, O Muhammad, you have an example in your brothers among the messengers, so do not let your people's denial of you lead you astray. As for the polytheists who denied the messengers, Satan made their actions seem attractive to them. So he is their protector today meaning they are under punishment and chastisement, and Satan is their protector and has no way to save them or help them, and they will have a painful torment. Then God the Almighty said to His Messenger: Indeed, the Book was only sent down to him to make clear to the people that over which they differ. So the Qur'an is a judge between people in everything over which they dispute. And guidance meaning for the hearts. And mercy meaning for those who hold fast to it. For a people who believe. Just as God the Almighty made the Qur'an a life for the hearts that are dead due to their disbelief, so He revives the earth after its death with what He sent down upon it from the sky of water. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen meaning who understand the words and their meaning.

16:66: God Almighty says: And indeed, for you O people, in the livestock which are camels, cows and sheep is a lesson meaning a sign and indication of the wisdom, power, mercy and kindness of their Creator. We give you drink from what is in their bellies He singled it out here, referring back to the meaning of blessings, or the pronoun refers back to the animal, for the livestock are animals, meaning We give you drink from what is in the belly of this animal, and in the other verse from what is in their bellies, and both are permissible, as in the Almighty's saying: "No indeed! It is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it" and in His saying: "And indeed, I am sending to them a gift and seeing with what the messengers return. So when Solomon came" meaning the money. And his saying: From between excrement and blood, pure milk means that the milk is separated from its whiteness, taste, and sweetness, between excrement and blood in the animal’s stomach, and each flows to its place when the food ripens in its stomach, so blood is diverted from it to the veins, milk to the udder, urine to the bladder, and excrement to the exit, and each of them does not mix with the other or blend with it after it separates from it, nor does it change with it. And His statement: Pure milk, palatable to those who drink it, meaning that no one will choke on it. And when He mentioned milk and that He, the Most High, made it a palatable drink for people, He followed it up with mentioning what people make of drinks from the fruits of palm trees and grapes, and what they used to make of intoxicating wine before it was forbidden. For this reason, He bestowed His favor upon them by saying: And from the fruits of palm trees and grapes you make intoxicant, indicating its permissibility in the Shari’ah before it was forbidden, and indicating equality between the intoxicant made from palm trees and that made from grapes, as is the doctrine of Malik, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and the majority of scholars. And likewise the ruling on all other drinks made from wheat, barley, corn and honey, as the Sunnah came with details of that, and this is not the place to expand on that. As Ibn Abbas said in his saying: Intoxication and good provision, intoxication is what is forbidden from their fruits, and good provision is what is permissible from their fruits. In another narration: Intoxication is forbidden, and good provision is permissible, meaning what is dried from them of dates and raisins, and what is made from them of coating, which is molasses, vinegar and wine, is permissible and is drunk before it hardens as the Sunnah has mentioned. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason. It is appropriate to mention the mind here, as it is the most noble thing in man. For this reason, God has forbidden this nation intoxicating drinks to protect their minds. God Almighty said: “And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and caused springs to gush forth therein, that they might eat of its fruit and of what their hands have made. Will they not then be grateful? Glory be to Him who created in pairs all things that the earth grows, and from themselves and from that which they do not know.”

16:68: What is meant by revelation here is inspiration and guidance, and the instruction for the bees to make homes in the mountains to which they take refuge, and in the trees and in what they build, then it is perfectly arranged and arranged so that there is no defect in its home, then God Almighty gave it a divine permission to make it subservient to eat from all the fruits, and to take the paths that God Almighty made easy for it, that is, easy for it wherever it wants in this great atmosphere, the vast wilderness, the valleys and the towering mountains, then each one of them returns to its home, not deviating from it to the right or to the left, but to its home and what it has in it of chicks and honey, so it builds wax from its wings and vomits honey from its mouth, and lays the chicks from its anus, then it goes to its pastures. Qatada and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: So follow the ways of your Lord submissively meaning obediently, so they made it a state of the one who is following. Ibn Zayd said: It is like the statement of God the Most High: And We have made them submissive to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat. He said: Do you not see that they move the bees in their homes from one country to another and they accompany them? The first statement is more apparent, which is that it is a state of the road, meaning so follow them submissively, Mujahid stated this explicitly. Ibn Jarir said: Both statements are correct. Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Shaiban ibn Farukh told us, Makin ibn Abd al-Aziz told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The lifespan of a fly is forty days, and all flies will be in the Fire except for the bee. God the Almighty says: There comes forth from their bellies a drink of varying colors in which there is healing for people. Between white, yellow, red, and other beautiful colors according to the differences in their pastures and food. His statement: In it is healing for people means in honey there is healing for people, that is, from the diseases that befall them. Some of those who spoke about prophetic medicine said: If he had said in it healing for people, it would have been a medicine for every disease. But he said in it healing for people, that is, it is good for everyone from cold diseases, because it is hot and a thing is treated with its opposite. Mujahid and Ibn Jarir said about his statement: Therein is healing for the people meaning the Qur’an, and this is a correct statement in itself, but it is not the apparent meaning here from the context of the verse, because the verse only mentions honey and Mujahid was not followed in his statement here, but what he said was mentioned in the statement of God the Almighty: And We send down of the Qur’an that which is healing and mercy for the believers and the statement of God the Almighty: O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers and the evidence that what is meant by the statement of God the Almighty: Therein is healing for the people is honey is the hadith narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Abu Al-Mutawakkil Ali bin Dawud Al-Naji on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that a man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My brother has diarrhea, so he said: Give him honey to drink. So he went and gave him honey to drink, then he came and said: O Messenger of God, I gave him honey to drink, but it only made his diarrhea worse. He said: Go and give him honey to drink. “Honey.” So he went and gave him honey to drink, then he came back and said: O Messenger of God, it only increased his diarrhea. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has spoken the truth and your brother’s stomach has lied. Go and give him honey to drink.” So he went and gave him honey to drink and he was cured. Some medical scholars said: This man had waste products, and when he gave him honey to drink while it was hot, they dissolved and rushed out, which increased his diarrhea. The Bedouin thought that this would harm him, but it was in his brother’s best interest. Then he gave him honey to drink, and the dissolution and expulsion increased. Then he gave him honey to drink and the same thing happened. When the corrupt waste products that were harmful to the body were expelled, his stomach remained stable, his temperament was improved, and the ailments and pains were expelled by the blessing of his advice. May the best prayers and peace be upon him from his Lord. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, liked sweets and honey. This is the wording of Al-Bukhari: And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Healing is in three things: in the incision of a cupper, or a drink of honey, or cauterization with fire. And I forbid my nation from cauterization.” Al-Bukhari said: Abu Naim told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “If there is any good in any of your medicines, or if there is any good in any of your medicines, then it is in the incision of a cupper, or a drink of honey, or a cauterization with fire that suits the disease, and I do not like to be cauterized.” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada on the authority of Jabir with it. Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, Saeed bin Abi Ayoub told us, Abdullah bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Khair, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir Al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three things that, if there is a cure for something, are: a cupping incision, a drink of honey, or cauterization that causes pain. But I hate cauterization and do not like it.” Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Harun bin Salul Al-Misri, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Muqri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Waleed, with the same wording: If there is a cure for something, then a cupping incision. He mentioned it, and this is a sound chain of transmission, but they did not include it. Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid bin Majah al-Qazwini said in his Sunan: Ali bin Salamah, who is al-Taghlabi, told us, Zaid bin Habbab told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Use the two cures: honey and the Qur’an.” This is a good chain of transmission that was transmitted by Ibn Majah alone, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Wakee’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is doubtful. We narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: If one of you wants to be healed, let him write a verse from the Book of God on a page, and wash it with rainwater, and let him take a dirham from his wife willingly, and buy honey with it and drink it, for it is healing: that is, from many aspects. God Almighty said: And We send down from the Qur’an that which is healing and mercy for the believers and He said: And We sent down from the sky blessed water and He said: But if they give you willingly anything of it, then take it in enjoyment and satisfaction and He said about honey: In it is healing for people. Ibn Majah also said: Mahmoud bin Khidash told us, Saeed bin Zakariya Al-Qurashi told us, Az-Zubayr bin Saeed Al-Hashemi told us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Salim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever licks honey three mornings every month, will not be afflicted with any great calamity. Az-Zubayr bin Saeed is rejected. Ibn Majah also said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Yusuf bin Sarh Al-Firyabi told us, Amr bin Bakir Al-Sakaski told us, Ibrahim bin Abi Ubla told us, I heard Abu Abi bin Umm Haram, who had prayed facing both qiblas, say: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: Use senna and sanut, for in them is a cure for every disease except death. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is death? He said: Death. Amr said: Ibn Abi Ubla said: Sanut is dill. Others said: Rather, it is the honey in the wineskin of ghee, and this is what the poet said: They are the butter of the year, there is no ambiguity about them, and they prevent the neighbor from getting angry. This is how Ibn Majah narrated it. His saying: There is no confusion in them means no mixing. His saying: They prevent the neighbor from oppressing them means oppressing and wronging them. His saying: Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought means that in God’s inspiration to these weak-born animals to undertake these tasks and to pick all kinds of fruits, then to collect them for wax and honey, which are among the best things, is a sign for a people who give thought to the greatness of their Creator, their Destiner, their Subject, and their Facilitator. They deduce from that that He is the Doer, the Able, the Wise, the All-Knowing, the Generous, the Merciful.

16:70: The Almighty tells us about His behavior towards His servants, and that He is the One who created them from nothingness and then after that He takes their souls, and some of them He leaves until they reach old age, which is weakness in creation, as God Almighty said: God is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength Al-Akhbar 2:17. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: The most decrepit age is seventy-five years, and at this age one experiences weakness of strength and senility, poor memory and little knowledge. For this reason, He said: So that after knowledge he may not know anything, meaning after he was knowledgeable he became ignorant of nothing due to weakness and senility. For this reason, Al-Bukhari narrated when interpreting this verse: Musa bin Ismail told us, Harun bin Musa Abu Abdullah Al-Awar told us on the authority of Shuaib on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate: I seek refuge in You from miserliness, laziness, old age, the most decrepit age, the torment of the grave, the trial of the Antichrist, and the trial of life and death. Zuhair bin Abi Salamah said in his famous Mu'allaqat. I am tired of the costs of life, and whoever lives eighty years without a father gets tired I saw fates striking blindly, whoever it hits dies, and whoever it misses lives and becomes old.
16:71: The Almighty shows the polytheists their ignorance and disbelief in what they claimed of partners for God, and they admit that they are His slaves as they used to say in their Talbiyah during their Hajj: Here I am, You have no partner except a partner who is Yours, You own him and what he owns. Then the Almighty said, denouncing them: You are not pleased to treat your slaves as equals in what We have provided for you, so how can He be pleased with His slaves being equals in divinity and glorification, as He said in the other verse: “He sets forth for you an example from among yourselves. Do you have among those whom your right hands possess partners in what We have provided for you? So you are equal in it. Do you fear them as you fear yourselves?” The verse. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: He says that they would not associate their slaves with their wealth and women, so how can they associate My slaves with Me in My authority? That is His saying: Then do they deny the favor of God? And he said in the other narration on his authority: How can you be pleased with Me that which you are not pleased with for yourselves. Mujahed said about this verse: This is like the false gods. Qatada said: This is a parable that God has given. Is there anyone among you who shares his wife and bed with his slave, and you equate God with His creation and His servants? If you are not satisfied with this for yourself, then God is more deserving of being exalted than you. And His statement: Do they then deny the favor of God? meaning that they have assigned to God a share of what He has created of crops and livestock, so they have denied His favor and associated others with Him. And on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, he said: Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, wrote this letter to Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari: Be content with your provision from this world, for the Most Gracious has favored some of His servants over others in provision, a trial with which He tests each one, so He tests the one for whom He has given provision in how he thanks God and fulfills the right that He has enjoined upon him in what He has provided for him and given him. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.
16:72: The Almighty mentions His blessings upon His servants by making for them from among themselves mates of their own kind and form. If He had made the mates from another kind, there would have been no harmony, love, or mercy. But out of His mercy, He created from the children of Adam males and females, and made the females mates for the males. Then the Almighty mentioned that He made from the mates sons and grandchildren, who are the sons’ children. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd. Shu’bah said on the authority of Abu Bishr on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas: sons and grandchildren, who are the son and the son’s son. Sunayd said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Abu Bakr on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Your children are those who take care of you, support you, help you, and serve you. Jameel said: The grandchildren were surrounded by the camels and their hands were covered with the camels’ crisis. Mujahid said: Sons and grandsons of his son and his servant. He said in another narration: The grandchildren are the helpers, assistants and servants. Tawus and others said: The grandchildren are the servants. Qatada, Abu Malik and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said the same. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: The grandchildren are those who serve you from your children and your children’s children. Ad-Dahhak said: The Arabs were only served by their sons. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement: And He has made for you from your wives sons and grandchildren means: The sons of a man’s wife are not from him. It is said: The grandchildren of a man work for a man. It is said: So-and-so is a grandchild for us, meaning he works for us. He said: Some men claimed that the grandchildren are the sisters of a man. This last one that Ibn Abbas mentioned was said by Ibn Masoud, Masrouq, Abu Ad-Dahha, Ibrahim An-Nakha’i, Saeed bin Jubayr, Mujahid and Al-Qurazi. Ikrimah narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are the in-laws. Ibn Jarir said: All of these sayings are included in the meaning of hafdah, which is service, from which His statement in Qunut: And to You we strive and we deliver. And since service may be from children, servants, and in-laws, the blessing is obtained by all of this, and for this reason He said: And He has made for you from your wives sons and grandchildren. I said: Whoever makes and grandchildren related to your wives, then what is meant must be the children and the children of the children and the in-laws, because they are the husbands of the daughters or the children of the wife. And this is what Al-Sha’bi and Al-Dahhak said, because they are usually under the protection of the man and in his lap and in his service. And this may be what is meant by his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, in the hadith of Nadrah ibn Aktham: And the child is your slave. Narrated by Abu Dawud. As for whoever makes hafdah servants, then according to him it is connected to His statement: And God has made for you from yourselves mates, meaning He has made for you the wives and children as servants. And His statement: And He has provided you with good things meaning food and drink. Then the Almighty said, denouncing those who associate others with Him in worshipping the Benefactor: Then do they believe in falsehood meaning rivals and idols and disbelieve in the favor of God meaning they conceal God’s favors upon them and attribute them to someone else. And in the authentic hadith: “God will say to the servant on the Day of Resurrection, praising him: Did I not marry you? Did I not honor you? Did I not subject horses and camels to you, and let you rule and sit?”
16:73: The Almighty says, informing about the polytheists who worshipped other than Him, even though He is the Benefactor, the Generous, the Creator, the Provider, alone, without partner. And despite this, they worship other than Him, idols, rivals, and statues that do not possess for them any provision from the heavens or the earth, meaning that they are not able to send down rain or cause crops or trees to grow, and they do not possess that for themselves, meaning that they do not have that, and they would not be able to do it if they wanted to. For this reason, the Almighty said: So do not make for God any comparisons, meaning do not make for Him rivals, likenesses, and counterparts. Indeed, God knows, while you do not know, meaning that He knows and bears witness that there is no god but Him, and you, in your ignorance, associate others with Him.
16:74: The Almighty says, informing about the polytheists who worshipped other than Him, even though He is the Benefactor, the Generous, the Creator, the Provider, alone, without partner. And despite this, they worship other than Him, idols, rivals, and statues that do not possess for them any provision from the heavens or the earth, meaning that they are not able to send down rain or cause crops or trees to grow, and they do not possess that for themselves, meaning that they do not have that, and they would not be able to do it if they wanted to. For this reason, the Almighty said: So do not make for God any comparisons, meaning do not make for Him rivals, likenesses, and counterparts. Indeed, God knows, while you do not know, meaning that He knows and bears witness that there is no god but Him, and you, in your ignorance, associate others with Him.
16:75: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This is a parable that God has given for the disbeliever and the believer. Qatada said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose it. The slave who is not able to do anything is like the disbeliever, and the one who is provided with good provision, so he spends from it secretly and openly, is the believer. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: It is a parable given for the idol and the Almighty Truth. Are these the same? Since the difference between them is apparent, clear and obvious, and only a fool would be ignorant of it, God the Almighty said: “Praise be to God. Rather, most of them do not know.”
16:76: Mujahid said: This also means the idol and the Almighty God means that the idol is mute, it does not speak or utter good or anything and is not able to do anything at all, so it has no speech or action, and with this it is all that means a dependant and a burden on its master Wherever He directs it meaning sends it it does not bring good and its efforts do not succeed Is it equal with these qualities and one who enjoins justice meaning fairness, so its speech is true and its actions are upright and he is on a straight path It was said: The mute is a client of Uthman, and this is what Al-Suddi, Qatadah, and Ata Al-Khurasani said, and Ibn Jarir chose this statement. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is an example for the disbeliever and the believer as well, as mentioned above. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan bin Al-Sabah Al-Bazzar told us, Yahya bin Ishaq Al-Salihini told us, Hammad told us, Abdullah bin Othman bin Khaitham told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ya`la bin Umayyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “God sets forth a parable: a slave owned by someone who has no power over anything,” he said: It was revealed about a man from Quraysh and his slave, meaning his statement: a slave owned by someone, the verse. And regarding his statement: “God sets forth a parable: two men, one of them mute and unable to do anything, and he is a burden on his master. Wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who enjoins justice and is on a straight path?” He said: He is Uthman bin Affan. He said: And the mute who, wherever he directs him, brings no good, he said: He is a client of Uthman bin Affan. Uthman used to spend on him and burden him and provide for him, and the other hated Islam and refused it and forbade him from giving charity and doing good, so it was revealed about them both. The Almighty says, denouncing the infidels who were at the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and who witnessed him and the guidance that God sent him with and the dazzling miracles with which God supported him. Yet, despite all of this, they were fleeing from him and dispersing from him, straying right and left, groups after groups, and sects after sects, as the Almighty said: Then why do they turn away from the reminder? * As if they were wild donkeys * Fleeing from a lion. This is similar to it, for God the Almighty said: Then what is the matter with those who disbelieved before you that they are rushing headlong? That is, what is the matter with these disbelievers who are with you, O Muhammad, that they are rushing headlong, that is, they are quickly fleeing from you, as Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Rushing headlong means setting off. To the right and to the left in groups. The singular is izza meaning scattered, and it is a state of rushing headlong that is, in the state of their dispersion and disagreement, as Imam Ahmad said about the people of desires, so they are opposing the Book, differing about the Book, and agreeing on opposing the Book. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then what is the matter with those who disbelieved before you that they are rushing headlong, he said, Before you, looking. “To the right and to the left in groups.” He said: The ‘izzin is the group of people, turning to the right and to the left, mocking him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu ‘Amir told us, Qurra told us on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: To the right and to the left in groups, that is, scattered, taking to the right and to the left, saying: What did this man say? Qatada said, Rushing deliberately, to the right and to the left in groups, meaning in groups around the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who have no interest in the Book of God or in His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ath-Thawri, Shu’bah, ‘Abtir ibn al-Qasim, ‘Isa ibn Yunus, Muhammad ibn Fadil, Waki’, Yahya al-Qattan, and Abu Mu’awiyah said, all on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of al-Musayyab ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Tamim ibn Tarfa, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to them while they were gathered together and said, Why do I see you gathered together? Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of al-A’mash with this chain of narration. Ibn Jarir said, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, Mu’ammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umair, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to his companions while they were gathered together and said, Why do I see you gathered together? This chain of narration is good, and I have not seen it in any of the six books from this source. God the Almighty says: Does every one of them aspire to enter a garden of pleasure? No! That is, do these people, in this state of their flight from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and their aversion to the truth, aspire to enter the gardens of pleasure? No, rather their refuge is Hell. Then God the Almighty says, confirming the occurrence of the Resurrection and the punishment they denied and ruled out, citing as evidence the beginning, which the return is easier than, and which they acknowledge. God the Almighty says: Indeed, We created them from that which they know. That is, from weak semen, just as God the Almighty said: Did We not create you from a despised water? And He said: “So let man consider from what he was created. He was created from a fluid ejected. Emerging from between the backbone and the ribs. Indeed, he is able to return him. On the Day when secrets will be exposed, he will have no power or helper.” Then God the Almighty says: So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests. That is, He who created the heavens and the earth, made the East and the West, and subjected the stars to appear in their Easts and set in their Wests. The meaning of the speech is that the matter is not as you claim, that there is no resurrection, no reckoning, no resurrection, and no rising again. Rather, all of that is real and will inevitably happen. That is why the letter la came at the beginning of the oath to indicate that what is sworn to is negation, which is the meaning of the speech and it is the refutation of their corrupt claim of denying the Day of Resurrection. They have witnessed from the great power of God the Most High what is more eloquent than establishing the Day of Resurrection, which is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the subjection of what is in them of creatures, animals, inanimate objects, and all kinds of existence. That is why God the Most High said: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know. And God the Almighty said: Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not weary in their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is over all things competent. And God the Almighty said in another verse: “Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing. * His command when He intends a thing is only to say to it, “Be,” and it is.” And He said here: So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests that We are surely Able * To substitute better than them, meaning on the Day of Resurrection We will return them with bodies better than these, for His power is suitable for that. And We are not to be outdone, meaning helpless, as God the Almighty said: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? Yes, We are Able to proportion his fingertips. And God the Almighty said: We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone * To substitute the likes of you and produce you in that which you do not know. Ibn Jarir chose To substitute better than them, meaning a nation that obeys Us and does not disobey Us, and he made it like His saying: And if We “If you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you. The first meaning is more evident, as other verses indicate it, and God Almighty knows best. Then the Almighty said: So leave them meaning O Muhammad to plunge into vain and play meaning leave them in their denial, disbelief and obstinacy until they meet their promised Day meaning they will know the consequences of that and taste its consequences On the Day they emerge from the graves in haste as if they were, toward a target, hastening meaning: They will rise from the graves when the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, calls them to the place of reckoning. They will rise in haste as if they were, toward a target, hastening. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: To knowledge they are striving. Abu Al-Aliyah and Yahya bin Abi Katheer said: To a goal they are striving towards. The majority of scholars have read to a target with a fat-ha on the noon and a sukoon on the sad, and it is a verbal noun meaning the accusative. Al-Hasan Al-Basri has read nab with a damma on the noon and the sad, and it is the idol, meaning it is as if in their haste to the place of standing, they would run to the target when they saw it in the world, hastening to see which of them would touch it first. This was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, Muslim al-Batin, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Abu Salih, Asim ibn Bahdalah, Ibn Zayd, and others. The Almighty’s statement, Their eyes will be humbled means submissive. Humiliation will overwhelm them means in response to their disdain for obeying in this world. That is the Day which they were promised. The end of the interpretation of Surah Sa’al. Praise and thanks be to God.
16:77: The Almighty informs about the perfection of His knowledge and His ability over things in His knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth and His exclusive knowledge of the unseen, so no one has access to that except that the Almighty informs him of what He wills, and in His perfect power that does not contradict or prevent, and that if He wills something, He only says to it, "Be," and it is, as He said: "And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye," meaning that what He wills is like the blink of an eye, and thus He said here: "And the command of the Hour is not but like the twinkling of an eye, or even nearer. Indeed, God is over all things competent," as He said: "He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul," then the Almighty mentioned His favor upon His servants in bringing them out of their mothers' wombs not knowing anything, then after this He grants them hearing by which they perceive sounds and sight by which they sense visible things and hearts, which are the minds whose center is the heart according to the correct view, and it was said: the brain and mind by which he distinguishes between things, their harm and their benefit, and these powers and senses are acquired by man gradually, little by little, whenever Zayd grew in hearing, sight and mind until he reached maturity. God Almighty created these in man so that he could use them to worship his Lord Almighty, so that he could use every limb, organ and strength to obey his Master. It was narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “God, the Almighty, says: ‘Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine has waged war against Me. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything better than performing what I have enjoined upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him. If he calls upon Me, I will surely answer him. If he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely protect him. I do not hesitate about anything I do as I hesitate about taking the soul of My believing servant. He hates death and I hate to offend him, but it is inevitable for him.” The meaning of the hadith is that if the servant is sincere in his obedience, all of his actions will be for God, the Almighty, the Majestic. He does not hear except for God, and he does not see except for God, meaning what God has prescribed for him. He does not strike or walk except in obedience to God, the Almighty, seeking help from God in all of that. This is why it was narrated in some narrations of the hadith in other than Sahih after his saying and his foot with which he walks. He walks with it, By Me he hears, by Me he sees, by Me he strikes, and by Me he walks. That is why the Almighty said: And He gave you hearing and sight and hearts that you might be grateful. Like His saying in the other verse: “Say, ‘It is He who created you and gave you hearing and sight and hearts. Little is it that you give thanks.’ Say, ‘It is He who multiplied you on the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.’” Then the Almighty alerted His servants to look at the birds subjected between the sky and the earth, how He made them fly with two wings between the sky and the earth in the atmosphere of the sky, and none holds them there except God with His Almighty power in which He placed powers that do that, and He subjected the air to carry them and the birds move likewise, as the Almighty said in Surat al-Mulk 67:“Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading out their wings and folding them in? None holds them up except the Most Gracious. Indeed, He is Seeing of all things.” And He said here: Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.

16:80: The Blessed and Exalted mentions the perfection of His blessings upon His servants in what He made for them of houses that are a dwelling for them, to which they take refuge, and in which they take shelter, and from which they benefit in all ways of benefit, and He also made for them houses from the hides of livestock, that is, from leather, which they carry lightly on their journeys, so that they may set them up for themselves in their residences, whether traveling or at home. For this reason, He said: You find them light on the day of your departure and the day of your residence, and from their wool meaning sheep, and their hair meaning camels, and their hair meaning goats, and the pronoun refers back to the livestock, furniture meaning you make furniture from it, which is money, and it was said: goods, and it was said: clothing, and the correct is more general than all of this, for furniture is made into rugs, clothes, and other things, and it is made into money and trade, and Ibn Abbas said: furniture is goods, and so said Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Atiyah Al-Awfi, Ata Al-Khurasani, Ad-Dahhak, and Qatadah. His saying: for a while means for a specified period and a known time. 16:84: God Almighty tells us about the affair of the polytheists on the Day of their Resurrection in the Hereafter, and that He will send from every nation a witness, who is its prophet, to testify against them regarding what they answered in what they conveyed to them from God Almighty: Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved meaning to apologize, because they know its falsehood and lies, like His saying: “This is a Day when they will not speak. Nor will permission be given to them to apologize.” That is why He said: “Nor will they be asked to repent. And when those who did wrong” meaning those who associated partners with God see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them meaning it will not be abated for them for a single hour. Nor will they be given respite, meaning, He will not delay them, but will quickly take them from the place of standing without reckoning. For when Hell is brought, it will be led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein seventy thousand angels. A neck of its will will look down upon the creation, and it will sigh so loudly that no one will remain except kneeling on his knees. It will say, I have been entrusted with every stubborn tyrant who has made another god with God, and so on and so forth. It will mention various types of people, as mentioned in the hadith. Then it will fold over them and pick them up from the place of standing as a bird picks up seeds. God the Most High said, “When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its roaring and groaning. But when they are thrown therein into a narrow place chained together, they will cry out there, ‘Destruction.’ Do not cry out today for a single destruction, but cry out for much destruction.” God the Most High said, And the criminals will see the Fire and think that they are falling into it, but they will find no escape from it. God the Most High said, “If only those who disbelieve knew when they will not be able to avert the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be aided. Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and confound them, and they will not be able.” He replied and they didn't even look. Then the Almighty informed about their gods’ disavowal of them when they were most in need of them, saying: And when those who associated others with God see their partners, meaning those whom they used to worship in this world, they will say, ‘Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You.’ So they will say to them, ‘Indeed, you are liars.’ That is, the gods will say to them, “You have lied. We have not commanded you to worship us,” as the Almighty said: “And who is more astray than he who calls upon those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their call, are unaware? And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship.” And the Almighty said: “And they have taken other gods besides God that they may be a source of honor for them. No! They will disbelieve in their worship and will be opponents to them.” And the Friend of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disbelieve in others, and the Almighty said: And it will be said, ‘Call upon your partners,’ and the verse, and there are many verses on this subject. And His statement: And on that Day they will submit to God in submission. Qatada and Ikrimah said: They will be humbled and surrendered on that Day, meaning they will all submit to God, so there will be no one who does not hear and obey. And like the statement of God the Most High: I will hear them and see them on the Day they come to Us. That is, I will not hear them and I will not see them on that Day. And He said: And if you could but see when the criminals will lower their heads before their Lord, ‘Our Lord, we have seen and heard.’ And He said: And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. That is, they will be submissive, humbled, submissive, repentant, and surrendered. And His statement: And on that Day they will submit to God in submission, and lost from them is that which they used to invent. That is, what they used to worship as an invention against God will be gone and vanished, so they will have no supporter, helper, or protector. Then God the Almighty said: Those who disbelieved and averted from the way of God - We will increase their punishment verse, meaning punishment for their disbelief and punishment for their averting people from following the truth, as God the Almighty said: And they forbid it and keep away from it meaning they forbid people from following it and keep away from it as well, And they destroy none but themselves, and they perceive not. This is evidence of the disbelievers’ varying degrees of punishment, just as the believers vary in their stations and degrees in Paradise, as God the Almighty said: He said, ‘For each is double, but you do not know.’ Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Surayj bin Yunus told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding God’s statement: We will increase their punishment over the punishment, he said: They were increased by scorpions whose fangs are like tall palm trees. Shureih bin Yunus told us, Ibrahim bin Sulayman told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, that he said: We have increased their punishment upon their punishment. He said: They are five rivers under the Throne, some of which they are punished with at night and some of which they are punished with during the day.

And like the statement of God the Most High: I will hear them and see them on the Day they come to Us. That is, I will not hear them and I will not see them on that Day. And He said: And if you could but see when the criminals will lower their heads before their Lord, ‘Our Lord, we have seen and heard.’ And He said: And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. That is, they will be submissive, humbled, submissive, repentant, and surrendered. And His statement: And on that Day they will submit to God in submission, and lost from them is that which they used to invent. That is, what they used to worship as an invention against God will be gone and vanished, so they will have no supporter, helper, or protector. Then God the Almighty said: Those who disbelieved and averted from the way of God - We will increase their punishment verse, meaning punishment for their disbelief and punishment for their averting people from following the truth, as God the Almighty said: And they forbid it and keep away from it meaning they forbid people from following it and keep away from it as well, And they destroy none but themselves, and they perceive not. This is evidence of the disbelievers’ varying degrees of punishment, just as the believers vary in their stations and degrees in Paradise, as God the Almighty said: He said, ‘For each is double, but you do not know.’ Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Surayj bin Yunus told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding God’s statement: We will increase their punishment over the punishment, he said: They were increased by scorpions whose fangs are like tall palm trees. Shureih bin Yunus told us, Ibrahim bin Sulayman told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, that he said: We have increased their punishment upon their punishment. 16:87: God Almighty tells us about the affair of the polytheists on the Day of their Resurrection in the Hereafter, and that He will send from every nation a witness, who is its prophet, to testify against them regarding what they answered in what they conveyed to them from God Almighty: Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved meaning to apologize, because they know its falsehood and lies, like His saying: “This is a Day when they will not speak. Nor will permission be given to them to apologize.” That is why He said: “Nor will they be asked to repent. And when those who did wrong” meaning those who associated partners with God see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them meaning it will not be abated for them for a single hour. Nor will they be given respite, meaning, He will not delay them, but will quickly take them from the place of standing without reckoning. For when Hell is brought, it will be led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein seventy thousand angels. A neck of its will will look down upon the creation, and it will sigh so loudly that no one will remain except kneeling on his knees. It will say, I have been entrusted with every stubborn tyrant who has made another god with God, and so on and so forth. It will mention various types of people, as mentioned in the hadith. Then it will fold over them and pick them up from the place of standing as a bird picks up seeds. God the Most High said, “When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its roaring and groaning. But when they are thrown therein into a narrow place chained together, they will cry out there, ‘Destruction.’ Do not cry out today for a single destruction, but cry out for much destruction.” God the Most High said, And the criminals will see the Fire and think that they are falling into it, but they will find no escape from it. We have not commanded you to worship us,” as the Almighty said: “And who is more astray than he who calls upon those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their call, are unaware? And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship.” And the Almighty said: “And they have taken other gods besides God that they may be a source of honor for them. No! They will disbelieve in their worship and will be opponents to them.” And the Friend of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disbelieve in others, and the Almighty said: And it will be said, ‘Call upon your partners,’ and the verse, and there are many verses on this subject. 16:89: God Almighty says, addressing His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And the Day We will raise up from every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We will bring you as a witness over these. He means your nation, that is, remember that day and its terror, and the great honor and lofty status that God granted you on that day. This verse is similar to the verse that Abdullah ibn Masoud concluded when he recited to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the beginning of Surat An-Nisa. When he reached the words: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you as a witness over these? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Enough. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: Then he turned and saw that his eyes were shedding tears. And His statement: And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things. Ibn Mas’ud said: In this Qur’an, He has explained to us all knowledge and everything. Mujahid said: All that is lawful and all that is unlawful. The statement of Ibn Mas’ud is more general and comprehensive, for the Qur’an includes all beneficial knowledge from report of what came before and knowledge of what will come, and all that is lawful and unlawful, and what people need in their worldly affairs, their religion, their livelihood and their afterlife. And guidance meaning for the hearts, and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims. Al-Awza’i said: And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things meaning: with the Sunnah. The reason for linking His statement: And We have sent down to you the Book with His statement: And We have brought you as a witness over these is that what is meant - and God knows best - is that the One who imposed upon you the conveyance of the Book that He revealed to you will ask you about that on the Day of Resurrection. Then We will surely question those to whom it was sent, and We will surely question the messengers. “By your Lord, We will surely question them all * About what they used to do.” “The Day when God will gather the messengers and say, ‘What was your response?’ They will say, ‘We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is the Knower of the unseen.’” And God Almighty said: Indeed, He who imposed upon you the Qur’an will bring you back to a place of return. Meaning, the One who imposed upon you the conveyance of the Qur’an will bring you back to it and bring you back on the Day of Resurrection and ask you about fulfilling what He imposed upon you. This is one of the sayings, and it is a good and correct one.
16:90: God the Almighty informs us that He commands His servants to be just, which is equity and balance, and He encourages us to do good, as He the Almighty says: "And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient." And He says: "The recompense for an evil is an evil like it. But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is due from God." And He says: And wounds are retaliation, but whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. And other verses indicating the legitimacy of justice and urging us to do good. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, God commands justice, he said: Testifying that there is no god but God. Sufyan bin Uyaynah said, justice in this context is the equality of the secret and the public of every worker for God's work, and goodness is that his secret is better than his public, and immorality and evil is that his public is better than his secret. And His statement: And giving to relatives means He commands us to maintain kinship ties, as He said: And give the relative his right and [also] the needy and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully. And His statement: And forbids immorality and wrongdoing. Immoralities are forbidden acts, and wrongdoings are those that are apparent from their doer. For this reason He said in another place: Say, ‘My Lord has only forbidden immoralities, such of them as are apparent and such as are concealed.’ As for oppression, it is aggression against people. It was stated in the hadith: There is no sin more deserving of God hastening its punishment in this world, along with what He has stored up for its doer in the Hereafter, than oppression and severing kinship ties. And His statement: He admonishes you means He orders you to do what He orders you to do of good and forbids you from what He forbids you from evil that you may remember. Al-Sha’bi said on the authority of Shatir ibn Shakl: I heard Ibn Mas’ud say: The most comprehensive verse in the Qur’an is in Surat al-Nahl 16:Indeed, God commands justice and doing good the verse, narrated by Ibn Jarir. Sa’id said on the authority of Qatadah: His statement: Indeed, God commands justice and doing good the verse: There is no good character that the people of ignorance used to do and approve of except that God commanded it, and there is no bad character that they used to taunt each other about except that God forbade it and presented it. Rather, He forbade the basest and most reprehensible character. I said This is why it came in the hadith: Indeed, God loves the highest morals and hates the lowest of them. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said in the Book of Knowledge of the Companions: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Fath al-Hanbali told us, Yahya ibn Muhammad, a client of Banu Hashim, told us, al-Hasan ibn Dawud al-Munkadri told us, Umar ibn Ali al-Muqaddami told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Umair, on the authority of his father, who said: Aktham ibn Saifi heard of the Prophet’s departure, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he wanted to go to him, but his people refused to let him go and said: You are our elder, you would not have gone to him. He said: Let someone come to him who will convey to him from me and who will convey to me from him. So two men volunteered and came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: We are the messengers of Aktham ibn Saifi, and he is asking you who you are, and what are you? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “As for who I am, I am Muhammad ibn Abdullah. As for what I am? I am the servant of God and His Messenger.” He said: Then he recited to them this verse: Indeed, God commands justice and doing good. The verse. They said: Repeat this statement to us. So he repeated it to them until they memorized it. Then they came to Aktham and said: He refused to mention his lineage. So we asked about his lineage and found him to be of noble lineage and of middle lineage in Mudar. He threw words at us that we had heard. When Aktham heard them, he said: I see that he commands good morals and forbids bad ones. So be leaders in this matter and do not be tails. A good hadith was narrated about its revelation, narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abu al-Nadr told us, Abdul Hamid told us, Shahr told us, Abdullah ibn Abbas told me: While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting in the courtyard of his house, Uthman ibn Maz’un passed by him and smiled at the Messenger of God. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Why don’t you sit down? He said: Yes, he said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat facing him, and while he was talking to him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked up to the sky. He looked up to the sky for a while, and began to lower his gaze until he placed it to his right on the ground. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from his companion, Uthman, to where he had placed his gaze, and began to shake his head as if he was understanding what was being said to him, and Ibn Maz’un was looking. When he had finished his need and understood what was being said to him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked up to the sky as he had looked the first time, and his gaze followed it until it disappeared into the sky. Then he came to Uthman in the same sitting position as before, and said: O Muhammad, while I was sitting with you, I never saw you do what you did this morning. He said: What did you see me do? He said: I saw you look up to the sky, then lower it to your right, and you turned to it and left me, and began to shake your head as if you were understanding something that was being said to you. He said: And you realized that? Uthman said: Yes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Messenger of God came to me just now while you were sitting. He said: The Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: So what did he say to you? He said: God commands justice and doing good the verse. Uthman said: “That was when faith was established in my heart and I loved Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” A good, connected, good chain of transmission in which continuous hearing is explained. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in an abbreviated form from the hadith of Abdul Hamid bin Bahram. Another hadith from Uthman bin Abi Al-Aas Al-Thaqafi on this matter. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Hureim told us, from Laith, from Shahr bin Hawshab, from Uthman bin Abi Al-Aas, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when his eyes fixed on him and he said: “Gabriel came to me and commanded me to put this verse in this place in this surah: ‘God commands justice and doing good’ the verse.” This is a good chain of transmission, and perhaps it is with Shahr bin Hawshab from both sources, and God knows best.
16:91: This is what God the Almighty commands, which is to fulfill covenants and agreements and to maintain confirmed oaths. For this reason, He said: And do not break oaths after confirming them. There is no contradiction between this and His statement: And do not make God an object of your oaths, the verse, and between His statement, the Almighty: “That is the expiation for your oaths when you swear. And guard your oaths,” meaning do not leave them without expiation. And between His statement, peace be upon him, in what was proven from him in the two Sahihs, that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “By God, if God wills, I will not swear an oath and then see something better than it, except that I will do what is better and absolve myself of it—and in another narration—and expiate for my oath.” There is no contradiction between all of this and the verse mentioned here, which is His statement: And do not break oaths after confirming them, because what is meant by these oaths is those included in covenants and agreements, not the oaths that are intended to urge or prohibit. For this reason, Mujahid said in His statement, And do not break oaths after confirming them. It means the oath, that is, the oath of the Age of Ignorance. It is supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated: Abdullah bin Muhammad - he is Ibn Abi Shaybah - told us, Ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Zakariya - he is Ibn Abi Zaydah - on the authority of Saad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jubayr bin Mut’im, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no oath in Islam, and whatever oath was made in the Age of Ignorance, Islam only increases its severity. Muslim narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibn Abi Shaybah with this same chain of transmission. Its meaning is that Islam does not require the oaths that the people of the Age of Ignorance used to make, for adhering to Islam is sufficient for what they were doing. As for what was reported in the two Sahihs on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made an alliance between the Muhajireen and the Ansar in our homes, what it means is that he established brotherhood between them and they inherited from each other until God abrogated that, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, Abdullah bin Musa told us, Abu Laila told us on the authority of Faridah regarding his statement: And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant, he said: It was revealed regarding the pledge of allegiance of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There were those who had accepted Islam who had pledged allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Islam, so he said: And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant, this is the pledge that you pledged to Islam, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, do not let the small number of Muhammad and the large number of polytheists lead you to break the pledge that you pledged to Islam. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Sakhr bin Juwairiyah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, who said: When the people deposed Yazid bin Muawiyah, Ibn Umar gathered his sons and family, then he testified, and then he said: As for what follows, we have pledged allegiance to this man on the pledge of allegiance to God and His Messenger, and I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “A banner will be raised for the traitor on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so. And among the greatest forms of treachery - unless it is associating partners with God - is for a man to pledge allegiance to another on the pledge of allegiance to God and His Messenger, then he breaks his pledge. So let none of you withdraw his hand, and let none of you be excessive in this matter, lest there be a rift between me and him.” The hadith attributed to him is in the two Sahihs. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abbas, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever stipulates a condition for his brother that he does not want to fulfill, is like one who extends his hand to his neighbor for no benefit. His statement, Indeed, God knows what you do, is a threat and warning to those who break their oaths after confirming them. His statement, And do not be like the one who untwists her spinning after it has been strong, Abdullah bin Katheer and As-Suddi said: This was a clumsy woman in Mecca who, whenever she spun something, would undo it after tightening it. Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: This is an example of someone who breaks his covenant after confirming it. This statement is more correct and clear, whether there was a woman in Mecca who untwisted her spinning or not. His saying: unraveled may be a verbal noun, she undid her spinning after it was strong meaning unraveled, and it may be a substitute for the predicate of was, meaning do not be unraveled, the plural of nakth from naqith, and for this reason he said after it: you take your oaths as a means of deception between you, meaning deception and trickery, that one nation should be more numerous than another nation, meaning you swear to people if they are more numerous than you so that they will feel secure with you, but if you are able to betray them, you betray them. So God forbade that in order to draw attention to the higher with the lower, if He forbade treachery in this case, then it is more appropriate for Him to forbid it with the ability and capacity. We have already mentioned - praise be to God - in Surat Al-Anfal the story of Muawiyah when there was a period of time between him and the king of the Romans. Muawiyah marched towards them at the end of the period, and when it expired and he was close to their country, he raided them while they were unaware and did not notice. Amr ibn Abasa said to him: God is Great, O Muawiyah, loyalty, not treachery. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever has a period of time between him and a people, let him not dissolve his contract until its period expires. So Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, returned with the army. Ibn Abbas said: That one nation is more numerous than another nation meaning more numerous. Mujahid said: They used to make alliances with allies and find that they were more numerous and more powerful than them, so they would break the alliance of these and make alliances with those who were more numerous and more powerful. So they were forbidden from doing that. Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said something similar. And His statement: God only tests you thereby Saeed ibn Jubayr said: He means by the number. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: That is, by His command to you to fulfill the covenant, And He will make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ, so He will reward every worker according to his work, good and evil.
