As for what was reported in the two Sahihs on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made an alliance between the Muhajireen and the Ansar in our homes, what it means is that he established brotherhood between them and they inherited from each other until God abrogated that, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, Abdullah bin Musa told us, Abu Laila told us on the authority of Faridah regarding his statement: And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant, he said: It was revealed regarding the pledge of allegiance of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There were those who had accepted Islam who had pledged allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Islam, so he said: And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant, this is the pledge that you pledged to Islam, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, do not let the small number of Muhammad and the large number of polytheists lead you to break the pledge that you pledged to Islam. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Sakhr bin Juwairiyah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, who said: When the people deposed Yazid bin Muawiyah, Ibn Umar gathered his sons and family, then he testified, and then he said: As for what follows, we have pledged allegiance to this man on the pledge of allegiance to God and His Messenger, and I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “A banner will be raised for the traitor on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so. And among the greatest forms of treachery - unless it is associating partners with God - is for a man to pledge allegiance to another on the pledge of allegiance to God and His Messenger, then he breaks his pledge. So let none of you withdraw his hand, and let none of you be excessive in this matter, lest there be a rift between me and him.” The hadith attributed to him is in the two Sahihs. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abbas, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever stipulates a condition for his brother that he does not want to fulfill, is like one who extends his hand to his neighbor for no benefit. His statement, Indeed, God knows what you do, is a threat and warning to those who break their oaths after confirming them. His statement, And do not be like the one who untwists her spinning after it has been strong, Abdullah bin Katheer and As-Suddi said: This was a clumsy woman in Mecca who, whenever she spun something, would undo it after tightening it. Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: This is an example of someone who breaks his covenant after confirming it. This statement is more correct and clear, whether there was a woman in Mecca who untwisted her spinning or not. His saying: unraveled may be a verbal noun, she undid her spinning after it was strong meaning unraveled, and it may be a substitute for the predicate of was, meaning do not be unraveled, the plural of nakth from naqith, and for this reason he said after it: you take your oaths as a means of deception between you, meaning deception and trickery, that one nation should be more numerous than another nation, meaning you swear to people if they are more numerous than you so that they will feel secure with you, but if you are able to betray them, you betray them. So God forbade that in order to draw attention to the higher with the lower, if He forbade treachery in this case, then it is more appropriate for Him to forbid it with the ability and capacity. We have already mentioned - praise be to God - in Surat Al-Anfal the story of Muawiyah when there was a period of time between him and the king of the Romans. Muawiyah marched towards them at the end of the period, and when it expired and he was close to their country, he raided them while they were unaware and did not notice. Amr ibn Abasa said to him: God is Great, O Muawiyah, loyalty, not treachery. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever has a period of time between him and a people, let him not dissolve his contract until its period expires. So Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, returned with the army. Ibn Abbas said: That one nation is more numerous than another nation meaning more numerous. Mujahid said: They used to make alliances with allies and find that they were more numerous and more powerful than them, so they would break the alliance of these and make alliances with those who were more numerous and more powerful. So they were forbidden from doing that. Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said something similar. And His statement: God only tests you thereby Saeed ibn Jubayr said: He means by the number. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: That is, by His command to you to fulfill the covenant, And He will make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ, so He will reward every worker according to his work, good and evil.
16:93: God Almighty says: And if God had willed, He could have made you O people one nation as He Almighty says: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together meaning He would have reconciled you and would not have created differences, hatred or enmity And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one nation; but they will not cease to differ * Except whom your Lord has mercy upon - and for that He created them, and likewise He says here: But He sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills then He will ask you on the Day of Resurrection about all your deeds and will reward you for them according to the smallest, smallest, and smallest. Then the Almighty warned His servants against taking oaths as a means of deception and trickery, lest a foot slip after it has been firmly established. This is like someone who was on the right path but then deviated from it and slipped from the path of guidance because of broken oaths that included turning away from the path of God. Because if the disbeliever sees that the believer has made a covenant with him and then betrayed him, he will no longer have any trust in the religion, and because of that he will turn away from entering Islam. For this reason He said, And taste the evil because you turned away from the path of God, and for you is a great punishment. Then the Almighty said: And do not exchange the covenant of God for a small price, meaning do not exchange faith in God for the worldly life and its adornments, for it is little, and if the son of Adam were to have the entire world, what is with God would be better for him, meaning the reward and recompense of God is better for the one who hopes in Him, believes in Him, seeks Him, and keeps His covenant, hoping for His promise. For this reason, He said: If you only knew * What is with you will be exhausted, meaning it will be emptied and come to an end, for it will have a limited, predetermined, and finite term. And what is with God is everlasting, meaning His reward for you in Paradise is everlasting, without interruption or exhaustion, for it is everlasting, does not change, and does not disappear. And We will surely reward those who are patient with the best of what they used to do, an oath from the Almighty Lord confirmed by the letter lam, that He will reward the patient with the best of their deeds, meaning He will overlook their bad deeds.

16:97: This is a promise from God Almighty to whoever does righteous deeds, which are deeds that follow the Book of God Almighty and the Sunnah of His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, whether male or female, from the children of Adam, and whose heart believes in God and His Messenger, and that this commanded deed is prescribed by God, so that God will grant him a good life in this world, and that He will reward him with the best of what he did in the Hereafter. The good life includes aspects of comfort from any aspect. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and a group that they interpreted it as lawful and good provision. And from Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he interpreted it as contentment, and so said Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Wahb bin Munabbih. Ali bin Abi Talhah said from Ibn Abbas: It is happiness. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: No one will have a good life except in Paradise. Ad-Dahhak said: It is lawful provision and worship in this world. Ad-Dahhak also said: It is working in obedience and being happy with it. The correct view is that the good life includes all of this. As it came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Saeed bin Abi Ayoub told us, Shurahbil bin Abi Sharek told me, on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has succeeded who has embraced Islam, has been provided with sufficient provision, and has been content with what God has given him. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah bin Yazid, who was recited by him. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Abu Hani’ from Abu Ali Al-Junbi, on the authority of Fadalah bin Ubaid, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: He has succeeded who has been guided to Islam, has sufficient provision, and is content with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a sahih hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God does not wrong the believer in the good deed he is given in this world and for which he is rewarded in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed with his good deeds in this world until when he passes to the Hereafter, he has no good deed for which he is given any good.” Narrated by Muslim.
16:98: This is an order from God the Almighty to His servants on the tongue of His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that if they want to recite the Qur’an, they should seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. This is a recommended matter, not an obligation. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir and other imams reported consensus on this. We have presented the hadiths that were narrated about seeking refuge in God in detail at the beginning of the interpretation, and praise and thanks be to God. The meaning of seeking refuge at the beginning of recitation is so that the reader’s recitation is not confused, or disturbed, and prevented from contemplating and thinking. For this reason, the majority were of the view that seeking refuge should be done before recitation. It was reported from Hamzah and Abu Hatim al-Sijistani that it should be done after recitation, and they used this verse as evidence. An-Nawawi narrated in his commentary on al-Muhadhdhab something similar from Abu Hurayrah as well, Muhammad ibn Sirin, and Ibrahim al-Nakha`i, and the first is the correct view because of the hadiths that were mentioned earlier indicating that it should be done before recitation. And God knows best. And His statement: Indeed, he has no authority over those who have believed and put their trust in their Lord. Ath-Thawri said: He has no authority over them to make them fall into a sin from which they will not repent. Others said: Its meaning is that he has no argument against them. Others said, like His statement: Except Your chosen servants among them. “His authority is only over those who take him as an ally.” Mujahid said: They obey him. Others said: They took him as a protector instead of God. And those who associate others with Him. That is, they associated others with Him in the worship of God. It is possible that the ba is a cause, that is, because of their obedience to Satan, they became polytheists with God. Others said: Its meaning is that he associated them with wealth and children.

16:101: The Almighty tells us about the weakness of the minds of the polytheists and their lack of steadfastness and conviction, and that it is inconceivable that they would believe while misery has been written for them. This is because when they saw the abrogating rulings being changed by abrogated ones, they would say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: You are only a fabricator, meaning a liar. Rather, it is the Almighty Lord who does what He wills and rules as He wills. Mujahid said: We replaced one verse with another, meaning We lifted it up and established another. Qatada said: It is like the Almighty's saying: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, the verse. Then the Almighty said, answering them: "Say, 'The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth,' meaning with truth and justice, 'to strengthen those who believe,' so that they believe in what was revealed first and second, and their hearts submit to it, 'and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims,' meaning He made it a guide and good tidings for the Muslims who believed in God and His Messengers.

16:103: The Almighty says, informing about the polytheists of what they were saying of lies, slander and calumny, that Muhammad who recites to us from the Qur’an is only taught by a human being, and they point to a foreign man who was among them, a slave of some of the clans of Quraysh, and he was a merchant who sold at Safa, and perhaps the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would sit with him and talk to him a little, and that was a foreigner who did not know Arabic, or he knew a little bit to the extent that he could respond to the address in what was necessary, so for this reason God the Almighty said, responding to their slander, The language of the one they refer to is foreign, and this is a clear Arabic language, meaning the Qur’an, meaning how can the one who brought this Qur’an learn in its eloquence, rhetoric and complete and comprehensive meanings that are more complete than the meanings of every book sent down to the children of the Messenger, how can he learn from a foreign man? No one with the slightest bit of intelligence would say this. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said in the biography: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - as far as I have been informed - often sat at Al-Marwah to pledge allegiance to a Christian boy called Jabr, a slave of some of the Banu Al-Hadrami, so God revealed: And We certainly know that they say, ‘It is only a human being who teaches him.’ The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language. And Abdullah bin Kathir said the same. And on the authority of Ikrimah and Qatadah: His name was Ya’ish. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Tusi told me, Abu Aamer told us, Ibrahim bin Tahman told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Abdullah al-Mala’i, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught a blacksmith in Mecca, and his name was Balaam, and he spoke a foreign language. The polytheists would see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entering and leaving him, so they said: Balaam is the one teaching him. So God revealed this verse: And indeed, we know that they say, ‘It is only a human being who teaches him.’ The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language. Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said: He is Salman al-Farsi. This statement is weak, because this verse is Meccan, and Salman only converted to Islam in Medina. Ubayd God bin Muslim said: We had two Roman slaves who would recite a book of theirs in their language, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pass by them and stand and listen to them. The polytheists said: He will learn from them. So God revealed this verse. Al-Zuhri said on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: The one who said that from the polytheists was a man who used to write the revelation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then he later apostatized from Islam and fabricated this statement. May God curse him.
16:104: God Almighty tells us that He does not guide those who turn away from His remembrance and neglect what He revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and who have no intention of believing in what came from God. God does not guide this type of people to believe in His signs and what He sent His Messengers with in this world, and they will have a painful and painful punishment in the Hereafter. Then God Almighty tells us that His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is not a slanderer or a liar, because only the worst of creation slanders against God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, those who do not believe in the signs of God from the infidels and atheists who are known for lying among the people. The Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the most truthful of people, the most pious, and the most perfect in knowledge, action, faith, and conviction. He was known for his truthfulness among his people, and none of them doubted that, to the extent that he was not called among them except the trustworthy Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. For this reason, when Heraclius, the king of the Romans, asked Abu Sufyan about those questions that he asked about the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he was among them: He said to him: Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he said? He said: No. Heraclius said: He would not have stopped lying to people and then gone and lied about God Almighty.

God does not guide this type of people to believe in His signs and what He sent His Messengers with in this world, and they will have a painful and painful punishment in the Hereafter. He said: No. Heraclius said: He would not have stopped lying to people and then gone and lied about God Almighty.
16:106: God Almighty informed about those who disbelieved in Him after believing and having insight, and whose hearts were opened to disbelief and who were reassured by it, that He became angry with them because of their knowledge of faith and then their turning away from it, and that they will have a great punishment in the Hereafter, because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter, so they committed what they committed of apostasy for the sake of this world, and God did not guide their hearts and make them steadfast in the true religion, so He sealed their hearts, so they do not understand anything that benefits them, and He sealed their hearing and their sight, so they do not benefit from them, nor did they avail them at all, so they are heedless of what is intended for them. There is no doubt meaning there is no doubt and no wonder that those of this description that in the Hereafter they are the losers meaning those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. As for His statement: Except for he who is forced while his heart is at rest with faith, it is an exception for those who disbelieved with their tongue and agreed with the polytheists with their words, forced by what they suffered of beating and harm, and their hearts refuse what He says, reassured by his faith in God and His Messenger. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that this verse was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir when the polytheists tortured him until he disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He agreed with them under duress and came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to apologize, so God revealed this verse. This is what Al-Sha’bi, Qatada, and Abu Malik said. He complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How do you find your heart? He said: Reassured by faith. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If they return, then return. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in a more simplified version, in which he cursed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spoke well of their gods. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, complained about that and said: O Messenger of God, I did not stop until I cursed you and spoke well of their gods. He said: How do you find your heart? He said: Reassured by faith, so he said: If they return, then return, and regarding that God revealed: Except for one who is forced and whose heart is at rest with faith. For this reason, the scholars agreed that the one who is forced to disbelieve is permitted to remain loyal in order to preserve his life, and he is permitted to refuse, as Bilal, may God be pleased with him, refused them that and they did to him deeds, to the point that they would place a huge rock on his chest in the intense heat, and they would order him to associate partners with God, but he refused them, and he would say: One, One. And he would say: By God, if I knew a word that was more vexing to you than that, I would say it, may God be pleased with him and satisfy him. Likewise, Habib bin Zaid Al-Ansari, when Musaylimah the Liar said to him: Do you bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God? He said: I do not hear. So he kept cutting him into pieces, and he was steadfast on that. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Ayoub told us on the authority of Ikrimah that Ali, may God be pleased with him, burned people who had apostatized from Islam. When Ibn Abbas heard about that, he said: I would not burn them with fire, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not punish with the punishment of God. And I would fight them with the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever changes his religion, kill him. When Ali heard about that, he said: Woe to the mother of Ibn Abbas. Narrated by al-Bukhari. He said: What is this? He said: A man was Jewish, then he converted to Islam, then he converted to Judaism, and we have wanted him to remain Muslim for I think two months. He said: By God, I will not stay until you strike off his head. So I struck off his head, and he said: God and His Messenger have decreed that whoever turns back from his religion, kill him, or he said: Whoever changes his religion, kill him. This story is in the two Sahihs with a different wording. It is better and more appropriate for a Muslim to remain steadfast in his religion even if it leads to his being killed, as Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Abdullah bin Hudhafah Al-Sahmi, one of the Companions, that the Romans captured him and brought him to their king, who said to him: Become a Christian and I will share my kingdom with you and marry you to my daughter. He said to him: Even if you gave me everything you own and everything the Arabs own on condition that I abandon the religion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the blink of an eye, I would not do it. He said: Then I will kill you. He said: You and that. He said: So he ordered him to be crucified, and he ordered the archers to shoot him close to his hands and feet while he offered him the religion of Christianity but he refused. Then he ordered him to be taken down. Then he ordered a pot, and in another narration a copper cow, to be heated. He brought a Muslim prisoner and threw him while he was looking, and behold, he was bones gleaming, and he offered him but he refused. So he ordered him to be thrown into it, so he was lifted into the pulley to be thrown into it, so he cried and desired it and called out to him, and he said: I only cried because my soul is only one soul that will be thrown into this pot at this moment for the sake of God, so I loved That I have a soul, as many as the hair on my body, that suffers this torment for the sake of God. In some narrations, he imprisoned him and prevented him from eating and drinking for days, then sent him wine and pork, but he did not approach it. Then he summoned him and said: What prevented you from eating? He said: It is permissible for me, but I would not let you gloat over me. The king said to him: Kiss my head and I will release you. He said: Will you release with me all the Muslim prisoners? He said: Yes. So he kissed his head and released him and released with him all the Muslim prisoners he had. When he returned, Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: It is the right of every Muslim to kiss the head of Abdullah ibn Hudhafah, and I will be the first. So he stood up and kissed his head, may God be pleased with them both.

16:111: These are another group who were oppressed in Mecca and humiliated by their people, so they agreed with them in the sedition. Then they were able to escape by emigrating, so they left their country, their families and their wealth seeking the pleasure and forgiveness of God, and they joined the ranks of the believers, and fought with them against the disbelievers, and were patient. So God the Almighty informed us that after that, that is, that action, which is the response to the sedition, He is Forgiving and Merciful to them on the Day of their Resurrection. The Day every soul will come to argue that is, argue for itself no one will argue on its behalf, neither a father nor a son nor a brother nor a wife. And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has done that is, of good and evil and they will not be wronged that is, the reward for good will not be reduced, nor will the reward for evil be increased, nor will they be wronged even a speck.
16:112: This is an example intended for the people of Mecca, for it was safe, secure and stable, and people were snatched away from around it, and whoever entered it was safe and not afraid, as God Almighty said: “And they said, ‘If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land. Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things, provision from Us?’” And thus He said here: Its provision comes to it in abundance meaning, pleasant and easy “from every place. So it denied the favors of God” meaning, it denied the favors of God upon it, the greatest of which was the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, as God Almighty said: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction * Hell, which they will burn in, and wretched is the settlement. For this reason, God changed their first two states to the opposite, and He said: So God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear meaning, He clothed it and made it taste hunger after the fruits of all things were brought to it, and its provision came to it in abundance from every place, and that is because They were stubborn with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and refused to do anything but contradict him, so he called upon them to suffer seven like the seven of Joseph, and a famine struck them that took away everything they had, so they ate the ‘alhaz, which is the camel’s hair mixed with its blood when they slaughtered it. And his saying: And fear is that they exchanged their security for fear of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions when they migrated to Medina from his power, his raids, and his armies, and he made everything they had in ruins and disgrace until God opened it for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was because of their actions, their transgression, and their denial of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom God sent among them from among them, and He bestowed His favor upon them in His saying: God has certainly conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves Al-Ma’idah 2:17. And the Almighty said: “So fear God, O you of understanding who have believed. God has sent down to you a message * A Messenger” 3:17, and His saying: “Just as We have sent among you a Messenger from among you who recites to you Our verses and purifies you and teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you that which you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me” 3:17. And just as the state of the disbelievers was reversed, so they feared after security, and went hungry after comfort, so God replaced the believers after their fear with security, and provided for them after poverty, and made them the leaders of the people, their rulers, their masters, their leaders, and their imams. What we said, that this example was given to the people of Mecca, was said by Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid, Qatadah, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam agreed with it, and Malik narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri, may God have mercy on them. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Nafi’ ibn Yazid told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Shuraih told us that Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith al-Hadrami told him that he heard Mushrah ibn Ha’an say: I heard Salim ibn ‘Atar say: We set out from Hajj with Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ‘Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was besieged in Madinah. She kept asking about him, What happened? Then she saw two riders, so she sent to them to ask them. They said, He was killed. Hafsah said, “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is the city about which God the Most High said, ‘God presents an example: a city that was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location. But it denied the favors of God. ’” Ibn Shuraih said: Ubaydullah ibn al-Mughira informed me on the authority of someone who told him that he used to say that it was Madinah.
16:113: This is an example intended for the people of Mecca, for it was safe, secure and stable, and people were snatched away from around it, and whoever entered it was safe and not afraid, as God Almighty said: “And they said, ‘If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land. Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things, provision from Us?’” And thus He said here: Its provision comes to it in abundance meaning, pleasant and easy “from every place. So it denied the favors of God” meaning, it denied the favors of God upon it, the greatest of which was the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, as God Almighty said: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction * Hell, which they will burn in, and wretched is the settlement. For this reason, God changed their first two states to the opposite, and He said: So God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear meaning, He clothed it and made it taste hunger after the fruits of all things were brought to it, and its provision came to it in abundance from every place, and that is because They were stubborn with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and refused to do anything but contradict him, so he called upon them to suffer seven like the seven of Joseph, and a famine struck them that took away everything they had, so they ate the ‘alhaz, which is the camel’s hair mixed with its blood when they slaughtered it. And his saying: And fear is that they exchanged their security for fear of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions when they migrated to Medina from his power, his raids, and his armies, and he made everything they had in ruins and disgrace until God opened it for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was because of their actions, their transgression, and their denial of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom God sent among them from among them, and He bestowed His favor upon them in His saying: God has certainly conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves Al-Ma’idah 2:17. And the Almighty said: “So fear God, O you of understanding who have believed. God has sent down to you a message * A Messenger” 3:17, and His saying: “Just as We have sent among you a Messenger from among you who recites to you Our verses and purifies you and teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you that which you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me” 3:17. 16:114: God the Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to eat His lawful and good provision and to thank Him for that, for He is the One Who bestows favors and favors them from the beginning, the One Who alone deserves to be worshipped, with no partner for Him. Then God the Almighty mentioned what He has forbidden them of what is harmful to them in their religion and their worldly life, such as dead animals, blood, and pork, and that which has been dedicated to other than God meaning slaughtered in a name other than God’s, and despite this, but whoever is forced to it, meaning in need without transgression or aggression, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. We have already discussed a verse similar to this in Surat Al-Baqarah, sufficiently enough so that there is no need to repeat it, and praise be to God. Then God the Almighty forbade following the path of the polytheists who permitted and prohibited merely because of what they described and agreed upon of names based on their opinions, such as al-Bahira, al-Sa’ibah, al-Wasila, al-Ham, and other than that, which was a law for them and which they innovated in their ignorance. He said: And do not say about what your tongues describe falsely, ‘This is lawful and this is unlawful,’ in order to invent a lie against God. This includes everyone who innovates an innovation for which he has no legal basis, or who permits something that God has forbidden, or who forbids something that God has permitted merely because of his opinion and desire. What is in His statement: When you describe is a source, meaning do not say a lie based on the description of your tongues. Then He threatened for that, saying: Indeed, those who invent a lie against God will not succeed, meaning in this world or in the Hereafter. As for in this world, it is a brief enjoyment, but as for in the Hereafter, they will have a painful punishment, as He said: We provide for them for a little while; then We force them to a severe punishment. He said: “Indeed, those who invent a lie against God will not succeed. Enjoyment in this world, then to Us.” Their return will be, then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.”

16:118: When God Almighty mentioned that He only forbade us dead animals, blood, pork, and that which was dedicated to other than God, and only permitted it in times of necessity - and in that there is an expansion for this nation for which God wants ease and does not want difficulty - God Almighty mentioned what He had forbidden to the Jews in their law before He abrogated it, and what they were in of constraint, restriction, shackles, and hardship, so He said: And to those who were Jews We forbade what We related to you before meaning in Surat Al-An’am in His statement: “And to those who were Jews We forbade them every animal with claws, and of the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fat, except what adhered to their backs or entrails or what was mixed with a bone. That is We recompensed them for their transgression, and indeed, We are truthful.” For this reason He said here: And We did not wrong them meaning in what We made difficult for them, but they were wronging themselves meaning, so they deserved that, like His statement: Then because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things which had been lawful to them and because of their averting from the way of God. “A lot.” Then the Almighty informed, out of His generosity and gratitude to the disobedient believers, that whoever among them repents to Him, He will accept his repentance, saying: Then indeed, your Lord is for those who did evil in ignorance. Some of the predecessors said: Everyone who disobeys God is ignorant. Then they repented after that and reformed. That is, they stopped what they were doing of sins and turned to doing good deeds. Indeed, your Lord, after that, that is, that action and slip, is Forgiving and Merciful.

16:120: God the Almighty praises His servant, messenger and friend Abraham, the leader of the monotheists and father of the prophets, and declares him innocent of the polytheists, Judaism and Christianity, saying: Indeed, Abraham was a nation, obedient to God, inclining toward truth. As for the nation, he is the leader who is followed, and the obedient is the humble and obedient, and the monotheist is the one who intentionally deviates from polytheism to monotheism, and for this reason He said: And he was not of the polytheists. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn: that he asked Abdullah ibn Masoud about the obedient nation, so he said: The nation is the one who teaches goodness, and the obedient is the one who obeys God and His Messenger, and on the authority of Malik, he said: Ibn Umar said: The nation is the one who teaches people their religion, and al-A'mash said on the authority of Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn, that he came to Abdullah and said: Who do we ask if we do not ask you? Ibn Masoud seemed moved by him, so he said: Tell me about the nation, so he said: The one who teaches people goodness. Al-Sha'bi said: Furwah bin Nawfal Al-Ashja'i told me: Ibn Mas'ud said: Mu'adh was a nation, obedient to God, and upright. I said to myself: Abu Abd Al-Rahman made a mistake and said that God said: Indeed, Abraham was a nation. He said: Do you know what a nation is and what an obedient person is? I said: God knows best. He said: A nation is one who knows good, and an obedient person is one who obeys God and His Messenger, and that is how Mu'adh was. It has been narrated from Ibn Mas'ud through other chains of narration, as narrated by Ibn Jarir. Mujahid said: A nation means a nation alone, and an obedient person is one who obeys. Mujahid also said: Abraham was a nation, meaning a believer alone, and all people at that time were disbelievers. Qatadah said: He was an imam of guidance, and an obedient person is one who obeys God. His statement: grateful for His favors means standing up to thank God for His favors upon him, like His statement: And Abraham who fulfilled meaning he carried out all that God commanded him to do. And His saying: He chose him means He selected him and selected him, as in His saying: And We had already given Abraham his sound judgment before, and We were of him Knowing. Then He said: And guided him to a straight path, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, according to an acceptable law. And His saying: And We gave him good in this world, meaning We gathered for him the best of this world from all that the believer needs to complete his good life, and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous. Mujahid said about His saying: And We gave him good in this world, meaning a tongue of truth. And His saying: Then We inspired you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, meaning from his perfection, greatness, and the soundness of his monotheism and his path, We have inspired you, O Seal of the Messengers and Master of the Prophets, to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists, as in His saying in al-An’am 6:Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists.’ Then the Most High said, denouncing the Jews.

16:124: There is no doubt that God Almighty has prescribed for every religion a day of the week on which people gather for worship. So God Almighty prescribed for this nation Friday because it is the sixth day on which God completed creation and on which His blessings were gathered and completed for His servants. It is said that God Almighty prescribed that for the Children of Israel through the tongue of Moses, but they turned away from it and chose Saturday because it is the day on which the Lord did not create any of the creatures that He completed their creation on Friday. So God Almighty obligated them to do so in the Torah, and He commanded them to adhere to it and to preserve it while commanding them to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he sent him and took their covenants and promises to do so. For this reason, God Almighty said: The Sabbath was only made obligatory for those who differed therein. Mujahid said: They followed him and abandoned Friday, then they continued to adhere to it until God sent Jesus, son of Mary. It is said that he changed them to Sunday. It is said that he did not abandon the Torah except for what was abrogated from some of its rulings, and that he continued to preserve the Sabbath until it was lifted, and that the Christians after him in During the time of Constantine, they were the ones who converted to Sunday in opposition to the Jews, and they converted to praying facing east of the rock, and God knows best. It was proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq from Muammar from Hammam from Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, but they were given the Book before us. Then this is their day which God imposed upon them and they differed about it, so God guided us to it. So the people will follow us on it: the Jews tomorrow and the Christians the day after tomorrow.” The wording of al-Bukhari. And on the authority of Abu Hurayrah and Hudhayfah may God be pleased with them both they said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God led astray those who came before us from Friday. The Jews had Saturday and the Christians had Sunday, so God brought us and guided us to Friday, so He made Friday, Saturday and Sunday. And likewise they will follow us on the Day of Resurrection. We are the last of the people of this world, and the first on the Day of Resurrection, and the judgment will be between them before all creation.” Narrated by Muslim.
16:125: God the Almighty says, commanding His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call people to God with wisdom. Ibn Jarir said: It is what He revealed to him from the Book and the Sunnah, and good preaching, meaning what it contains of deterrents and events for people, reminding them of them so that they may beware of the wrath of God the Almighty. And His statement: And argue with them in a way that is best, meaning whoever among them needs to debate and argue, let it be with a good face, gentleness, kindness, and good speech, like His statement: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, the verse. So God the Almighty commanded him to be gentle, just as He commanded Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, when He sent them to Pharaoh, in His statement: And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear. And His saying: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way verse, meaning that He knows who among them is wretched and who is happy, and He has written that down and finished it. So call them to God and do not let yourself be consumed by regret over those among them who have gone astray, for it is not your responsibility to guide them, you are only a warner, upon you is the message and upon Us is the reckoning. Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, “It is not your responsibility to guide them, but God guides whom He wills.”
16:126: God Almighty commands justice in retaliation and equality in fulfilling rights, as Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Ath-Thawri on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, that he said regarding the words of God Almighty: Then punish with the like of that with which you were punished, if a man takes something from you, then take the like of it, and this is what Mujahid, Ibrahim, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Ibn Zaid said: They had been ordered to forgive the polytheists, but powerful men converted to Islam and said: O Messenger of God, if God gives us permission, we will be victorious over these dogs. So this verse was revealed, then it was abrogated by Jihad. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of some of his companions on the authority of Ata bin Yasar who said: Surat An-Nahl was revealed in its entirety in Mecca, and it is Meccan except for three verses from the end of it that were revealed in Medina after Uhud when Hamza, may God be pleased with him, was killed and mutilated. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If God gives me victory over them, I will mutilate thirty men from them. When the Muslims heard that, they said: By God, if we gain victory over them, we will mutilate them in a way that no Arab has ever mutilated anyone before. Then God revealed: And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were punished to the end of the surah. This is a mursal hadith and it contains an unknown man who was not named. This was narrated from another connected source. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Amr bin Asim told us, Salih Al-Mari told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood over Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, may God be pleased with him, when he was martyred. He looked at a sight that was more painful to the heart than any sight he had ever seen, or he said to his heart. He looked at him and he had mutilated him, and said: “May God’s mercy be upon you. I only knew you to be a maintainer of kinship and a doer of good deeds. By God, were it not for the grief that follows you, I would be happy to leave you until God gathers you from the bellies of wild beasts - or a word similar to it. By God, I will mutilate seventy like you.” Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with this Surah and recited: And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were punished to the end of the verse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disbelieved, meaning about his oath, and refrained from doing that. This is a weak chain of transmission, because… Salih is Ibn Bashir Al-Mari, who is weak according to the imams. Al-Bukhari said: He is a fabricator of hadith. Al-Sha’bi and Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed regarding the Muslims’ statement on the day of Uhud regarding those who were mutilated, We will mutilate them. So God revealed that about them. Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said in his father’s Musnad: Hadiya bin Abdul Wahhab Al-Marwazi told us, Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, Isa bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Abu bin Ka’b, who said: When the day of Uhud came, sixty men from the Ansar were killed, and six from the Muhajireen, so the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If we have a day like this from the polytheists, we will outdo them. When the day of the conquest came, a man said: Quraysh will not be recognized after today, so a crier called out: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has granted security to the black and the white except for so-and-so and so-and-so - people he named - so God Almighty revealed: And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted to the end of the surah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We will be patient and not punish. This noble verse has examples in the Qur’an, for it includes the legitimacy of justice and the exhortation to virtue, as in His statement: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it then He said: But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with God the verse. He said: And wounds are retaliation. Then he said: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. And he said in this verse: And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. Then he said: But if you are patient, it is better for the patient. And the Almighty’s saying: And be patient, and your patience is not but through God is an emphasis on the command to be patient and an announcement that this can only be achieved by the will of God, His help, His power and His strength. Then the Almighty said: And do not grieve over them meaning over those who oppose you, for God has decreed that. And do not be in distress meaning grief over what they are plotting meaning over what they are exerting themselves to be hostile to you and bring evil to you, for God is sufficient for you, your supporter, your helper, your helper, and your victor over them. And His saying: Indeed, God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good means with them through His support, victory, assistance, guidance and effort. This is a special companionship, like His saying: When your Lord inspired to the angels, ‘I am with you, so strengthen those who believe’ and His saying to Moses and Aaron: Do not fear, indeed, I am with you, hearing and seeing and the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Abu Bakr while they were in al-Kahf 18:Do not grieve, indeed, God is with us. As for the general companionship, it is through hearing, sight and knowledge, like His saying, the Most High: And He is with you wherever you are, and God is Seeing of what you do and His saying, the Most High: “Have you not seen that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? There is not a secret conversation between three but that He is their fourth, nor five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are” and as God Almighty said: And you are not engaged in any matter, nor do you recite from it any Qur’an, nor do you do any deed but that We are witnesses over you and the meaning of those who fear Him is that they abandoned the forbidden things, and those who are… “Muhsinun” means they did acts of obedience. These are the ones whom God protects, guards, supports, aids, and grants them victory over their enemies and opponents. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, Misa’ar told us on the authority of Awn on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hattab: Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was among those who feared God and were muhsinun. The last interpretation of Surat An-Nahl. Praise and thanks be to God, and may God’s prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, his family, and his companions.
